item.title: [Yardbarker] Dodgers Make Sudden Freddie Freeman Announcement
item.dc:creator: Simeon Kotto
item.description: Freddie Freeman is back where the Los Angeles Dodgers like him: in the middle of a loaded order, on the last afternoon of the regular season. After sitting Saturday against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers first baseman is in Sunday’s Game 162 lineup at Oracle Park and batting third. The card posted by Underdog MLB puts Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter, Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freeman at first, Kyle Tucker in right, Teoscar Hernández in left, Max Muncy at third, Andy Pages in center, H
item.content:encoded:
Freddie Freeman is back where the Los Angeles Dodgers like him: in the middle of a loaded order, on the last afternoon of the regular season.
After sitting Saturday against the San Francisco Giants, the Dodgers first baseman is in Sunday’s Game 162 lineup at Oracle Park and batting third.
The card posted by Underdog MLB puts Shohei Ohtani at designated hitter, Mookie Betts at shortstop, Freeman at first, Kyle Tucker in right, Teoscar Hernández in left, Max Muncy at third, Andy Pages in center, Hunter Feduccia behind the plate and Tommy Edman at second. Jack Dreyer is listed as the starter in what figures to be a bullpen game.
The off day was not a surprise. Freeman had started each of the previous 10 games and was dragging a .522 OPS over 45 plate appearances in that stretch.
Enrique Hernández filled in at first on Saturday while the club gave its 37-year-old cornerstone a breather.
That is how Dave Roberts has handled September: keep Freeman available, not exhausted, with the postseason a few days away.
Sunday’s assignment is the one Freeman has occupied for most of his career.
He has started more than 1,300 games in the three-hole across Atlanta and Los Angeles, and even after spring talk about a cleanup role behind Tucker, the Dodgers keep sliding him back between Betts and the middle of the order when they want their most reliable left-handed bat seeing traffic.
He entered the weekend hitting .290 with 167 hits, 16 homers and 70 RBIs. The power has been quieter lately — he has gone without an extra-base hit for more than two weeks — but the bat-to-ball skill is still the reason Los Angeles trusts him with runners on.
The context around the lineup is October-minded. Los Angeles is 99-62 and chasing a 100-win season in the finale. Will Smith is the only everyday starter sitting.
Blake Treinen is headed to the injured list with a shoulder issue, so the bullpen will be asked to work. First pitch is 12:05 p.m. PT / 3:05 p.m. ET on SportsNet LA.
For Freeman, the message is simple. One rest day. Then back in the three-hole, glove at first, with Ohtani and Betts in front of him and Tucker behind him.
If the Dodgers are going to finish 100-62 and carry momentum into the NLDS, they want their veteran first baseman in the middle of it — not on the bench, and not buried in the order.
Sunday is a tune-up with meaning: one more look at the group that has to win in October.

item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

27 Sep 2026, 21:25 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Darren Yamashita)
The Los Angeles Dodgers will look to tarnish the final game of longtime San Francisco Giants broadcaster Mike Krukow's career with a 100th regular-season win when the California rivals wrap up the regular season on Sunday afternoon.
The finale in San Francisco will send the Dodgers (99-62) on their quest for a third consecutive World Series championship and Krukow into retirement after 36 years of calling Giants games.
Also a pitcher for the Giants for the final seven of his 14 seasons in the majors, Krukow, 74, will be honored after Sunday's game, in which the home team will seek to end a four-game losing streak overall and a seven-game skid against the Dodgers.
'I'm going to tell them just how much they mean to me and my family,' Krukow promised this week about his farewell speech. 'I don't know if you can convey it in words, but it'll be conveyed in emotion. That I can guarantee.'
Krukow was in the booth when San Francisco won three World Series titles in five seasons from 2010-14, but the team has been to the postseason just twice since then (2016, 2021), losing both times in the National League Division Series. This season, the Giants (65-96) will finish with their fewest wins in a full season since going 64-98 in 2017.
Meanwhile, the Dodgers will wind up with more wins than the 98 they had in 2024 and 93 last season, regular seasons followed by World Series victories. This will be their 14th consecutive appearance in the postseason; they also won the World Series in the pandemic-shortened season in 2020.
With a first-round bye to start their three-peat effort as a result of having the second-best record in the National League, the Dodgers will need 11 wins to achieve a first in Major League Baseball since the Yankees captured the World Series in 1998, 1999 and 2000.
Los Angeles saw a lot go right in its first two games in San Francisco -- both victories -- as they got home runs from Teoscar Hernandez, Andy Pages, Enrique Hernandez and Mookie Betts, sharp starting pitching from Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell, and stellar game-closing from Tanner Scott.
The Dodgers will take the field Sunday with postseason roster spots still up for grabs and pitchers needing one more outing before a five-day break leading into a best-of-five NLDS, which will open in Los Angeles on Saturday.
'We want to finish playing good baseball,' Dodgers manager Dave Roberts told reporters. 'Our guys still got to get ready because we've got a week of not playing baseball. So (the goal is) just to finish strong, finish the season out.'
One unresolved issue for Los Angeles in the postseason is who will bat leadoff.
Shohei Ohtani, who manned the spot almost exclusively while healthy earlier in the season, led off Friday's 2-0 win over the Giants, going 0-for-4 with three strikeouts.
Roberts moved Betts into the top spot for Saturday's 4-3 victory, and while Betts went just 1-for-5 with a strikeout, his hit was his 23rd home run of the season.
Ohtani, who singled and struck out twice while slotted second on Saturday, has gone just 4-for-18 with just one extra-base hit, a double, since returning from a 16-day absence due to discomfort in his right biceps.
While the Dodgers have not announced a starting pitcher for Sunday's game, the Giants will send right-hander Carson Seymour (0-2, 4.70 ERA) to the mound as an opener. He will make his first start after 24 relief appearances this season.
Seymour does not have a decision in five career outings against the Dodgers. He has a 3.60 ERA, allowing two runs in five innings. He pitched the sixth inning on Saturday, striking out one.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [ocregister.com] Kiké Hernandez’s 9th-inning blast lifts Dodgers past Giants again
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett

item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO — It was a four-inning wellness check.
Pitching for the first time since he left his start in Cincinnati after one inning with groin muscle discomfort, Blake Snell passed his test. He allowed one run on five hits in his four innings Saturday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 4-3 on Kiké Hernandez’s ninth-inning home run.
The Dodgers will finish the season with a chance to reach 100 victories for the first time since 2023 – but the fourth time in the past six seasons and sixth time in the past nine full seasons.
Snell was healthy if not efficient. He threw 77 pitches to get through his four innings, allowing hits in each inning.
“Definitely needed to pitch today. Definitely showed that,” Snell said. “I was trying to go up and in, I was missing up and away. Even the last pitch of the game, I try to go up and in and miss right down the middle. I don’t know the last time I did that. It’s been a while. Even the changeup, the speed was up to 88. I gotta fix that as well. Get that to 86. Curveball, the release just has to get better.
“But overall, I learned a lot from it. Really encouraged by it, and just happy to get my legs underneath me and get going and completely move past the groin. I mean, it felt great today, and the velo was good. … I’ve got to figure my body out a little more, but I got a week to do so, and I’m really looking forward to that.”
He stranded runners at the corners in the first inning and at second base in the second. Jonah Cox led off the third with a double into the left-field corner, stole third and scored on a sacrifice fly. Snell gave up a two-out single in the fourth, but Shay Whitcomb was thrown out by left fielder Teoscar Hernandez when he tried to stretch it into a double.
After the game in Cincinnati, Snell expressed confidence that he had avoided serious injury by recognizing the signs early and coming out of the game – something he didn’t do before landing on the injured list four previous times with groin injuries.
Saturday supported that decision. Snell’s fastball averaged 96.8 mph (up slightly from his season average) and he got 10 swings-and-misses (though only three strikeouts). Snell now lines up as the likely Game 3 starter in the National League Division Series, giving him over a week before his next start.
“I thought the fastball was had life. Just some near misses to kind of flip counts,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “The changeup was okay. The curveball I thought was good. But I think for him overall, he just wasn’t as efficient as he wanted, as we wanted. But again, I thought it was fine for his last tune-up for the postseason.
“I was confident, we were confident (that Snell was healthy). But I think it’s still good to see it. And it’s good also that we got it out of the way, got that rust off, versus whatever game in the postseason, then he’s rusty, and you’ve got to kind of pick up the pieces in a playoff game. So I thought today it was again, really best-case scenario.”
The Dodgers’ offense gave Snell a 3-1 lead.
Mookie Betts hit a solo home run in the third inning – his seventh home run in September as he surges over the final month of the season. Four singles and a walk produced two more runs in the fourth inning.
After a two-hit game including an RBI double Thursday, Shohei Ohtani has gone 1 for 9 with five strikeouts in the two games against the Giants. The lone hit was a ground ball under the glove of Giants first baseman Brett Harris in the fourth inning that was originally ruled an error and later changed.
“I thought today there was just more chase,” Roberts said of Ohtani’s 1 for 5. “And I don’t know if he’s trying to get hits, find his swing, getting a little over-anxious. Everything from Shohei to the training staff, the hitting guys, the work has been great. Looks exactly like it did, like it’s supposed to look.”
Roberts dismissed any suggestion that Ohtani is still not healthy after spending two weeks on the injured list.
“I don’t see any wincing. The bat speed is still (good),” Roberts said. “There’s one thing to just say you could just put him on ice and hope that the performance is there Game One of the postseason, or there’s another camp that says everything looks right and you have to get him (at-bats) and it’s still only – what is it 12, 13 at bats, 14 at bats (since he returned)? So, with a long layoff, that’s not easy either to come back and perform.”
The Dodgers’ bullpen couldn’t hold the 3-1 lead. The Giants came back to tie it with single runs against Brock Stewart in the seventh and Evan Phillips in the eighth before Hernandez put the Dodgers back in the lead with a leadoff home run in the ninth.
The homer was an uplifting moment in a difficult season for Hernandez, who started the season on the IL following elbow surgery, returned for two games, then missed two months with an oblique injury.
“Yeah, I mean it’s been tough, but I mean, it is what it is,” Hernandez said. “That’s the card I’ve drawn this year. It’s nobody’s fault. I was expected to miss the first couple months because of my rehab, and then I was not expecting to miss more time so quickly after coming back. It just happened to be that way. And when you have a team like this one, it’s hard getting in the lineup. So it’s just one of those things where that’s what you have, and you got to make the best of it. I just happened to not have made the best of my opportunities this year.”

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers face the San Francisco Giants in the second game of the regular season’s final series.
The Dodgers will rotate in veterans with something to provide heading into the postseason, with Freddie Freeman notably absent for Saturday’s game.
Dodgers Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Shohei Ohtani, DH
3. Will Smith, C
4. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Miguel Rojas, 3B
7. Andy Pages, CF
8. Kike Hernandez, 1B
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
The Dodgers are facing lefty Matt Wilkinson, which lets Rojas and Kike Hernandez enter the mix in a favorable matchup with a righty-heavy lineup.
The biggest note of the game is that once again, Mookie Betts is batting leadoff, while Shohei Ohtani is hitting second.
Manager Dave Roberts has made it clear that Ohtani wasn’t guaranteed to hit leadoff against lefties, and with Betts continuing to deliver quality plate appearances, the Dodgers skipper is willing to start the order with Betts.
At-bats from Andy Pages, Kike Hernandez, Miguel Rojas, and Tommy Edman are all worth monitoring. Pages is still somewhat fresh off the injured list, while Tommy Edman has been in a slump.
Rojas and Hernandez feature so inconsistently that they are always worth following whenever they play.
Who is pitching for the Dodgers?
Blake Snell starts against the Giants after being pulled early in his last outing. Snell, who has a history of groin injuries, had some groin soreness surface against the Cincinnati Reds last week.
Initial concern about his postseason viability grew, and as a key member of the rotation, the Dodgers could ill-afford to lose him.
The injury doesn’t seem major, and Snell has a chance to get some pitching work before October kicks into high gear.
In terms of actual pitching production, Snell sits at the top, with elite stuff and sharp command.
If he is fully sharp, Snell can carry a team in the postseason, and while the Dodgers don’t need that this week, next week will be a different story.

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Josue De Paula defensive concerns may not be a long-term Dodgers fear
item.dc:creator: Pat Ragazzo
item.description: There has been a lot of talk lately surrounding the defensive concerns of Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder and top prospect Josue De Paula. However, his outfield defense might not be a worry at all in the long-term. De Paula, 21, appeared in 11
item.content:encoded:
There has been a lot of talk lately surrounding the defensive concerns of Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder and top prospect Josue De Paula. However, his outfield defense might not be a worry at all in the long-term.
After getting called up to make his MLB debut on September 11, the Dodgers' No. 1 prospect, who is Baseball America's No. 4 prospect on their Top 100 list, only saw six innings in left field with the rest of his playing time coming as the designated hitter.
De Paula, 21, appeared in 11 games and slashed .323/.500/.581 with a 1.081 OPS, one home run, and seven RBI. He replaced Shohei Ohtani, but was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City on September 23 once Ohtani returned from the IL.
Why the Dodgers shouldn't be concerned with Josue De Paula's defense
With Ohtani back healthy for the playoffs, De Paula would likely have to pinch-hit or play the outfield in order to see time in October if he is selected to the postseason roster. But can the Dodgers trust De Paula in left field?
Per Baseball America, multiple scouts project De Paula as a 30-grade defender on the 20-to-80 scouting scale. His reads and routes to the ball have been described as "shaky" and he is not considered to be very rangy out there either.
As one Dodgers person put it, "De Paula's defense is a work in progress, but if you saw him play, you would come away knowing he's perfectly capable of being an average defender."
The same Dodgers person pointed out that there were similar concerns about center fielder Andy Pages when he was coming up through the minors. Pages has since become a Gold Glove caliber defender in the major leagues.
De Paula is currently in Triple-A, where he is playing left field in preparation of possibly being chosen to the Dodgers' playoff roster. Optioning De Paula was more so to help him continue the development of his outfield defense before the postseason. Although he had his struggles in the outfield during the minor league season this year, De Paula has looked fine in left field since being sent back down.
Why the Dodgers should carry De Paula on their postseason roster
There appears to be a strong chance that De Paula makes the Dodgers' postseason roster as a bench player over catcher Dalton Rushing, who can only hit due to a partially torn UCL and flexor strain in his throwing elbow.
For that, the logical choice seems to be for the Dodgers to carry De Paula on their playoff roster over Rushing. De Paula made an impact with his bat in his brief stint in the majors and showed Los Angeles a glimpse of his potential and what's to come, which could be future stardom.
The Dodgers could decide to platoon the left-handed hitting De Paula with righty slugger Teoscar Hernandez in left field in their pursuit of a third straight World Series title. And Hernandez's defense in left isn't that strong to begin with, neither is Kyle Tucker's in right field.
When looking at it from a future lens, with Hernandez having one more year left on his contract, De Paula is likely to become the Dodgers' everyday left fielder by 2028 given Ohtani is locked in as the DH for the foreseeable future. And as far as De Paula's defensive concerns go, they are seemingly exaggerated at this point.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Praises Tarik Skubal after Dodgers' Shutout Win
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Dave Roberts has seen plenty of outstanding pitching performances this season, but Friday night’s masterpiece from Tarik Skubal was something special. The Dodgers manager had little hesitation when asked whether Skubal’s seven shutout innings against the Giants represented his finest outing since joining the club. “That was the best we’ve seen,” Roberts said following the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory at Oracle Park. “He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was worki
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA — Dave Roberts has seen plenty of outstanding pitching performances this season, but Friday night’s masterpiece from Tarik Skubal was something special. The Dodgers manager had little hesitation when asked whether Skubal’s seven shutout innings against the Giants represented his finest outing since joining the club.
“That was the best we’ve seen,” Roberts said following the Dodgers’ 2-0 victory at Oracle Park. “He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working, and he just went after those guys and did a fantastic job.”
“Pounded the zone. Everything was working tonight. Efficient. I think he went through seven innings, 75 pitches, something like that. Incredibly good.”
Skubal Had Something to Prove
Skubal had been less than pleased with his previous outing against the Giants, when he surrendered 10 hits and struggled with his fastball command. Roberts believes that disappointment helped fuel Friday’s extraordinary performance.
“I think so, yeah. He wasn’t pleased with his outing the last time, and so to come back and face the same team and do what he did less than a week later is pretty impressive.”
Asked what makes Skubal’s fastball so difficult for hitters, particularly when he’s attacking the strike zone as aggressively as he did Friday, Roberts pointed to the combination of velocity, deception and secondary pitches.
“When it’s right, it’s an explosive fastball. He stays behind it well. He hides it well, and then he’s got the secondaries to go with it.”
“Tonight certainly was really dominant with the fastball and essentially could do whatever he wanted tonight.”
Roberts Sees an Improved, More Confident Roki Sasaki
Skubal’s departure after seven innings provided another opportunity for Roki Sasaki to demonstrate what he can contribute to the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen. The young right-hander struck out two in a scoreless eighth inning, and Roberts believes he’s considerably further along than he was at this point last season.
“Yeah, he is. I think the fastball’s better. I think the split’s better, and it’s also nice that he’s already done it.”
“So just in total, he’s just a better pitcher than he was last year and a lot more confident. Certainly, the stuff was really good the last couple outings.”
Sasaki was followed by Tanner Scott, who struck out two in a perfect ninth inning to record his 24th save. Roberts liked the combination, although he was careful to avoid committing himself to specific bullpen roles for October.
“I liked it tonight. They both did a fantastic job.”
“It’s just better to have as many guys that you have confidence in in leverage. It allows us to deploy guys whenever we need to.”
“I feel comfortable with a lot of guys at the back end, for sure.”
The Offense Needs Contributions Beyond Its Superstars
The Dodgers managed just two runs Friday, both coming on solo home runs in the second inning. Although the offense has struggled to string together hits over the past several games, Roberts remains encouraged by the quality of the team’s at-bats.
“I thought obviously we had two homers tonight. Will had a really good night. I thought Mookie still looks fine.”
“We’re not putting a bunch of hits together, but it doesn’t seem like the results are there. I still like our intent in the batter’s box.”
“Try not to overthink it as far as the production the last few games, because honestly, I like where our offense is at mentally. But I do think, like I said before, this week for our group is going to be a very good thing.”
The manager also emphasized the importance of getting production from the middle and bottom of the batting order. With opposing teams likely to focus their attention on Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman, players like Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages will have opportunities to make a considerable difference.
“It certainly adds length. As we all know, when you get to the postseason, they’re going to try to eliminate Sho and try to make other guys beat you.”
“It always sort of comes to the middle to the bottom of the order, where you’ve either got to get guys on base or get hits, get big hits.”
“The way Teo’s been swinging, Andy’s swinging, we’ve got to get Tommy on track. It’ll certainly be helpful.”
Pages Is Entering October in a Much Different Place
Roberts admitted that he’s been somewhat surprised by how quickly Pages has regained his form after missing approximately five weeks with an injury. Playing in just his fourth game since returning from the injured list, Pages collected two hits Friday, including his 22nd home run.
“I am a little bit, but in the other sense, I’m not surprised because he put in a lot of work before he was active to really hit the ground running.”
“Even the jumps defensively, covering so much ground out there, the at-bat quality. You think that when you take five weeks off, your timing is going to be off a little bit, but he put in a lot of time.”
Asked about Pages’ struggles during last year’s postseason and what might be different this time around, Roberts pointed to the young outfielder’s confidence.
“I think the one thing is the confidence. He went into last October really scuffling, and it sort of bled into October.”
“Right now, he feels really confident, swinging the bat well, and the hope is that this one bleeds into October as well.”
“His headspace is just a lot more confident this year.”
Roberts Still Likes What He Sees From Ohtani
Ohtani went hitless with three strikeouts Friday, but Roberts indicated that he’s continuing to see encouraging signs from the slugger following his return from the injured list.
“Loved them. I liked them. He’s fine.”
“I really think that, just for me, the swing decisions, the bat speed, that’s kind of all that. If that’s in place, then the results will be there.”
With the first-round bye already secured, the Dodgers have the opportunity to use their final regular-season games to sharpen their approach and prepare for the NLDS.
Friday’s performance offered plenty of encouragement on the pitching side, particularly from Skubal and Sasaki. And with Teoscar and Pages continuing to swing the bats well, Roberts has reason to believe his club is moving in the right direction as October approaches.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 2-0, on Friday night and improved to 98-62 on the year.
Two-time Cy Young award winner Tarik Skubal unleashed another masterpiece with seven scoreless innings, 10 strikeouts, no walks and just three hits allowed. Offensively, Will Smith had a three-hit evening while two second inning solo home runs were collected by Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages (his first home run since being activated off the injured list).
Ahead of Friday's game, the Dodgers demoted an infielder to make room on the roster to activate catcher Dalton Rushing. Manager Dave Roberts spoke on the kind of role fans can expect from Rushing down the stretch.
“At the most it would be three pinch-hit at-bats, so just conduct at-bats and see what you got,” Roberts said. “Just the circumstances of his situation, it’s just tough to just be hurt, come back, then be hurt again, and then take three pinch-hit at-bats to potentially then say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.’"
Additionally, Roberts had a message for rookie Josue De Paula after he was optioned to Triple-A following a productive first 11 games at the major league level. The reasoning, he revealed, was that De Paula could act as a spark plug while superstar Shohei Ohtani was on the injured list — and during his time on the shelf, it's exactly what the 21-year-old provided.
“This was the original thought, that once Shohei gets back, we’re going to send him out,” Roberts said. “We had a runway to give him, which we gave him and he performed more than admirably. This also, as far as the timing, just gives us an opportunity to potentially have him back for the postseason. He’s a part of the conversation, and he’s earned that, and that’s what I told him last night.”
Finally, there is an update on southpaw Blake Snell after he lasted just one inning due to groin discomfort during his most recent start. Luckily for Dodgers fans, the team announced that Snell will make his next scheduled start on Saturday during the penultimate regular season game.

item.description: Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages hit home runs, Skubal strikes out 10 as Dodgers beat Giants 2-0 Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the San Francisco Giants SAN FRANCISCO -- Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning to back Tarik Skubal's three-hit, seven-inning performance, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 2-0 on Friday night. Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with three
item.content:encoded:
Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages hit home runs, Skubal strikes out 10 as Dodgers beat Giants 2-0
Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning, leading the Los Angeles Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the San Francisco Giants
SAN FRANCISCO -- Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages hit home runs in the second inning to back Tarik Skubal's three-hit, seven-inning performance, and the Los Angeles Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants 2-0 on Friday night.
Shohei Ohtani went 0 for 4 with three strikeouts in his third game back after a 13-game stint on the injured list because of right biceps discomfort.
Skubal (12-7) struck out 10, including four straight during one stretch, and didn't walk a batter in his 10th start for the two-time defending World Series champions since being acquired from Detroit on Aug. 2. The Dodgers had won each of his previous six outings as he went 4-0 over his last four decisions spanning six starts since a loss to Milwaukee on Aug. 16.
It was the two-time reigning AL Cy Young Award winner's fourth double-digit strikeout game of the season, second with Los Angeles.
Roki Sasaki pitched a perfect eighth with a pair of strikeouts before Tanner Scott finished the one hour, 53 minute game for his 24th save. It was the second-fastest game in the ballpark's 27-year history and the fastest Giants-Dodgers game since a 1:50 contest on Aug. 30, 1958, in the second game of a doubleheader, according to MLB.
Giants starter Yunior Marte (0-2) surrendered the two home runs among his six hits in five innings. Earlier in the day, San Francisco welcomed back former closer Camilo Doval, claimed off waivers after they dealt him to the Yankees ahead of the 2025 trade deadline.
Manager Dave Roberts gave utility man Tommy Edman a day off to rest and planned to sit some regulars or give them shorter stints in Sunday's regular-season finale.
Los Angeles has won six straight against the Giants and is 7-4 this year to capture the season series for a fifth straight season, going 47-22 during that time.
The Dodgers have held opponents to four or fewer runs in 108 games, going 82-26 in those contests.
LHP Blake Snell (4-1, 1.86 ERA) pitches Saturday against his former Giants team, which counters with LHP Matt Wilkinson (1-3, 3.65).
___

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Commentary: Dodgers' three-peat hopes rest on their four aces — and bottom-of-order production
item.dc:creator: Bill Shaikin
item.description: - Click here to listen to this article - - The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load. - In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs. - Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after c
item.content:encoded:
- Click here to listen to this article
-
- The Dodgers’ path to a third straight World Series title will depend on four frontline starters, but manager Dave Roberts hopes his offense won’t leave them carrying the load.
- In a 2-0 win over San Francisco, Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages offered a timely reminder that the Dodgers will need consistent production from the bottom half of the lineup in the playoffs.
- Hernández is a proven October hitter, while Pages is finding his swing after coming back from a broken hand.
SAN FRANCISCO — This is the 60th anniversary of the 1966 World Series, in which the losing team did not score for the final 33 innings of the series.
That losing team was the Dodgers. Over the final three games of the series, Jim Palmer, Wally Bunker and Dave McNally of the Baltimore Orioles each pitched a complete-game shutout.
That art of pitching is not in style today. Yoshinobu Yamamoto pitched two complete games last October, but he cannot pitch every game, even if he left that impression upon the Toronto Blue Jays.
The Dodgers’ clearest and cleanest route to a three-peat nonetheless rests upon the four shoulders of Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow. If the four aces can do to October opponents what the 1966 Orioles did to the Dodgers, or some reasonable 21st century facsimile, we’ll see you at the parade.
Does Dodgers manager Dave Roberts believe his starting pitchers will have to carry the load in October?
“I hope not,” Roberts said.
Tarik Skubal gives up just three hits and strikes out 10 in his final start before the postseason to help carry the Dodgers to a 2-0 win over the Giants.
Friday’s 2-0 victory over the San Francisco Giants offered two encouraging swings. Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages each hit home runs, a reminder that a properly tuned Dodgers offense runs on more than Shohei Ohtani, Mookie Betts, Freddie Freeman and Will Smith.
Skubal scattered three hits and struck out 10 in seven scoreless innings, which would have gone for naught without the Hernández and Pages home runs. Given that the Dodgers were playing the Giants and the remains of their depleted roster, it was something of a warning sign: this could happen against a postseason team.
No team can plan to score a lot of runs against the Dodgers’ starters. The opposing game plan would be to neutralize them and keep the game close enough to where one or two big swings can make the difference. The Giants, who have the National League’s second-worst record, almost pulled it off.
“When you get to the postseason, they’re going to try to eliminate Shohei and try to make other guys beat you,” Roberts said. “So it always sort of comes to the middle to the bottom of the order, where you’ve either got to get guys on base or get hits, get big hits.”
In October, Hernández is who you want at bat. He has homered in six of the seven postseason series he has played for the Dodgers, including each of the last five. In 33 postseason games for the Dodgers, he has driven in 25 runs.
For most players, offensive production drops in October, when batters face the best pitchers from the best teams. For Hernández, his career OPS is .796 in the regular season and .792 in the postseason.
And, for all his summer struggles, he is batting .354 this month, with an OPS just shy of 1.000. He’ll be, as the league-issued hoodies used to say, October ready.
For Pages, however, last October was cruel.
This October was not looking particularly promising, either. Pages missed 27 games because of a broken hand, leaving him the final six games of the regular season to get his swing back into rhythm.
“You think that you take five weeks off,” Roberts said, “that your timing is going to be off a little bit.”
So far, so good: five hits in 12 at-bats, including the home run Friday.
Pages ended the regular season last year with four hits in his final 28 at-bats. That, Roberts said, tells him this October will be different for Pages.
“I think the one thing is the confidence, how he went into last October really scuffling, and it sort of bled into October,” Roberts said, “where I think right now he feels really confident, swinging the bat well, and the hope is that this one bleeds into October as well.
“So, I think it’s definitely a different result going into October, and then also his headspace. There’s a lot more confidence this year.”
In 2025, when the Dodgers won the World Series, they ranked second among the 30 major league clubs in runs scored, and in home runs. In 2024, when they won the World Series, they ranked third in runs scored, and in home runs.
The Dodgers rank fourth in runs scored this year, and seventh in home runs. The offense is down some, if not much. In all the national postseason hype, the Dodgers projections will boil down to one sentence: Can anyone stop those starters?
“I think at first glance that’s what you see in our ballclub,” Roberts said. “But we have a lot of talented, really good hitters and I hope they work hand in hand and not just our pitching and defense carry us.”
For the Dodgers, the postseason opens one week from Saturday. If the Dodgers roll out the 1966 playbook, their October stay will be short.

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers blanquean a Giants 2-0 con jonrones de Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pages
Tarik Skubal ponchó a 10 bateadores en siete entradas y permitió apenas tres hits para liderar la victoria de Los Ángeles sobre San Francisco.
Los Angeles Dodgers vencieron 2-0 a los San Francisco Giants este viernes, impulsados por los jonrones de Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pages en la segunda entrada y una destacada actuación del lanzador Tarik Skubal.
Skubal permitió apenas tres hits en siete entradas, ponchó a 10 bateadores y no concedió boletos. El lanzador consiguió así su victoria número 12 de la temporada y mejoró su registro a 12-7.
Fue la décima apertura de Skubal con los Dodgers desde que el equipo lo adquirió de los Detroit Tigers el 2 de agosto. Los Ángeles ha ganado sus seis aperturas anteriores y el lanzador acumula un registro de 4-0 en sus últimas cuatro decisiones, que abarcan seis aperturas.
El actual ganador del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana consiguió además su cuarto partido de la temporada con al menos 10 ponches, el segundo desde su llegada a Los Ángeles.
Hernández y Pages aportaron los únicos batazos de Los Ángeles
Los Dodgers construyeron toda su ventaja en la segunda entrada.
Teoscar Hernández conectó el primero de los dos cuadrangulares y, posteriormente, Andy Pages también envió la pelota fuera del parque para colocar el marcador 2-0.
El abridor de San Francisco, Yunior Marte, permitió los dos jonrones entre los seis imparables que concedió durante cinco entradas. Marte cargó con la derrota y dejó su récord en 0-2.
Sasaki y Scott completaron la blanqueada
Después de la salida de Skubal, Roki Sasaki lanzó una octava entrada perfecta y ponchó a dos bateadores.
Tanner Scott se encargó del noveno inning y consiguió su salvamento número 24 de la temporada.
El encuentro duró apenas una hora y 53 minutos, convirtiéndose, según MLB, en el segundo partido más rápido disputado en los 27 años de historia del estadio de San Francisco. También fue el juego entre Dodgers y Giants más rápido desde un encuentro de una hora y 50 minutos disputado el 30 de agosto de 1958.
Ohtani sigue buscando ritmo tras su regreso
Shohei Ohtani terminó de 0-4 con tres ponches en su tercer partido desde que regresó de la lista de lesionados, donde permaneció 13 juegos debido a molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Los Dodgers, por su parte, han ganado seis partidos consecutivos contra los Giants y tienen marca de 7-4 frente a San Francisco esta temporada, con lo que aseguraron la serie de temporada por quinta campaña consecutiva.
Durante ese período de cinco temporadas, Los Ángeles tiene un registro de 47-22 contra los Giants.
Snell abrirá el sábado
Los Dodgers continuarán la serie este sábado con el zurdo Blake Snell, quien tiene marca de 4-1 y una efectividad de 1.86.
Snell se enfrentará a su antiguo equipo, mientras que San Francisco enviará al montículo al zurdo Matt Wilkinson, con récord de 1-3 y efectividad de 3.65.

item.title: [MLB.com] Skubal cruises before Sasaki, Scott prep for postseason roles
item.dc:creator: Sonja Chen

But after throwing seven scoreless innings on 75 pitches, the southpaw was shaking hands and receiving hugs in the visitors' dugout at Oracle Park. item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO -- Tarik Skubal was showing no signs of slowing down in what was shaping up to be his most dominant start as a Dodger. But after throwing seven scoreless innings on 75 pitches, the southpaw was shaking hands and receiving hugs in the visitors' dugout at Oracle Park.
Skubal struck out 10, gave up just three hits and faced two batters over the minimum in his final regular-season start on Friday night.
His pitch count was in such a good spot that he could have made a bid for the second "Maddux" of his career. But when the bottom of the eighth inning came around, Skubal remained in the dugout and Roki Sasaki relieved him on the mound.
“That was the best we’ve seen," manager Dave Roberts said. "He was on a mission tonight. You could see it. Everything was working. He just went after those guys and did a fantastic job."
While Roberts has maintained that the Dodgers won't approach their final games of the season differently with the No. 2 postseason seed locked in, the 2-0 win over the Giants was an example of how having nothing left to play for changes the calculus of in-game decisions.
With five days off before the NL Division Series begins on Oct. 3 at Dodger Stadium, Roberts isn't necessarily looking to use this weekend for load management. But these final games are the Dodgers' last opportunity to try out players in their postseason roles in a lower-stakes environment.
Had this game taken place a week ago, Skubal may have stayed in to finish off his gem. But the Dodgers had already planned on having Sasaki pitch on Friday, and with only two additional games remaining for him to prepare for his postseason bullpen role, they opted not to deviate from that plan.
Sasaki got his work in, tossing a 1-2-3 eighth inning with two strikeouts in his second appearance back from the injured list. Tanner Scott closed out the victory, the Dodgers' 98th of the season -- which could be a hint at how both leverage arms will be used in the postseason.
"It’s better to have as many guys as you have confidence in in leverage," Roberts said. "So it just allows us to deploy guys whenever we need to."
For much of Skubal's two months as a Dodger, both he and the team maintained that they had not seen him at his best on the mound. Not only was Friday his best performance yet with L.A., but it came against a team that had frustrated him just six days earlier.
Last Saturday, Skubal lasted only five innings while allowing four runs against the Giants at Dodger Stadium. He bemoaned his lack of fastball command, which he believed was the main factor behind the disappointing results.
Skubal didn't just have command of his fastball on Friday. He had command of everything, throwing 60 of his 75 pitches for strikes and going 21-for-23 in first-pitch strikes. He generated 21 whiffs on 43 swings (48.8%), including a season-high 12 on his fastball.
"I think it's the key to who I am. I think it makes me who I am," Skubal said. "I don't know how many pitches I threw tonight, but felt like there were only like 14 or 15 balls out of however many throws. … I'm not going to do that every time, but I think that just speaks to conviction and the pitch-calling."
Said Giants manager Tony Vitello: "He’s going to come right at you, so maybe we could have been a little more aggressive early. But the bottom line is, he was sharper than the other night [in L.A.], and maybe we weren’t as sharp."
While Skubal received minimal run support -- solo homers from Teoscar Hernández and Andy Pages in the second inning -- he had no issues holding the line.
Along with Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Blake Snell and Tyler Glasnow, Skubal is part of the four-man gauntlet the Dodgers will run out in October. In his final tuneup, he looked postseason-ready, and then some.
"Once the months change and the playoffs start, nothing matters," Skubal said. "It's just about winning that game, and that's how I treat every single start. Because I'm just trying to put our team in a position to win a baseball game, and that won't change from today and whenever my next start is."

item.content:encoded:
Los Dodgers blanquean a los Gigantes con 2 jonrones y 10 ponches de Skubal
SAN FRANCISCO — Teoscar Hernández y Andy Pagés conectaron jonrones en la segunda entrada para respaldar la actuación de Tarik Skubal, quien permitió tres hits en siete innings, y los Dodgers de Los Ángeles vencieron 2-0 a los Gigantes de San Francisco la noche del viernes.
Shohei Ohtani se fue de 4-0 con tres ponches en su tercer juego de regreso tras una estadía de 13 partidos en la lista de lesionados debido a molestias en el bíceps derecho.
Skubal (12-7) ponchó a 10, incluidos cuatro consecutivos durante un tramo, y no otorgó bases por bolas en su décima apertura con los bicampeones defensores de la Serie Mundial desde que fue adquirido de Detroit el 2 de agosto. Los Dodgers habían ganado cada una de sus seis salidas anteriores, mientras él tuvo marca de 4-0 en sus últimas cuatro decisiones a lo largo de seis aperturas desde una derrota ante Milwaukee el 16 de agosto.
Fue el cuarto juego de la temporada del ganador vigente en dos ocasiones del premio Cy Young de la Liga Americana con ponches de doble dígito, el segundo con Los Ángeles.
Roki Sasaki lanzó un octavo inning perfecto con un par de ponches antes de que Tanner Scott cerrara el juego, que duró una hora y 53 minutos, para su 24to salvamento. Fue el segundo juego más rápido en los 27 años de historia del estadio.
El abridor de los Gigantes, el dominicano Yunior Marte (0-2), permitió los dos jonrones entre los seis hits que concedió en cinco innings. Más temprano en el día, San Francisco dio la bienvenida de regreso al ex cerrador Camilo Doval, reclamado en waivers después de que lo traspasaran a los Yankees antes de la fecha límite de cambios de 2025. ___

item.content:encoded:
El campocorto de los Dodgers de Los Ángeles, Mookie Betts, está teniendo un septiembre demente en el plato y parece alguno que puede sobrellevar la ataque en la postemporada.
El demente septiembre de Betts
Betts está bateando .367 en septiembre hasta el viernes, con 21 carreras impulsadas, seis jonrones y nueve dobles.
Tiene un OPS de 1.117 y un wRC+ de 219, ambas métricas resaltan cuán elitista ha sido. Ha sido, con diferencia, su mejor mes de la temporada y es similar a sus mejores marcas como MVP.
Anuncio
Da boletos el 16% de sus apariciones en el plato y se poncha sólo el 8,5% de las veces.
Su enfoque en el plato luce excelente, con buenas decisiones de swing y un esforzado dominio de la zona de strike que empuja a los lanzadores a realizar lanzamientos más desafiantes de los que desearían.
Cuando hace swing, tiene 32 bolas aceptablemente golpeadas este mes y la velocidad de salida promedio es de 92.6 mph, la más entrada del año hasta el momento.
Por qué los Dodgers necesitaban esta producción de Betts
Para sorpresa de nadie, Betts fue el mejor bateador del equipo en septiembre. Su wRC+ solo rivaliza con Josue De Paula, aunque el tamaño de su muestra fue mucho más pequeño que el de Betts.
Anuncio
Shohei Ohtani se perdió la viejo parte del mes por una ultraje en el padrino derecho, mientras que Andy Pages asimismo se perdió la viejo parte del mes y regresó solo en los últimos días.
Por otra parte, Freddie Freeman y Tommy Edman se han vuelto prácticamente fríos, lo que solo aumenta aún más la escazes de que alguno dé un paso al frente.
Betts ha sido el hombre que ha llevado la ataque, con 25 carreras ponderadas creadas, según FanGraphs, la viejo cantidad en el equipo, superado por Teoscar Hernández, quien tiene 19.
Con su surgimiento y la caída de Edman, Betts asumió el puesto de primer bate hasta que Ohtani regresó, y su maniobra ha sido tan bueno que incluso luego del regreso de la superestrella japonesa, el manager Dave Roberts todavía mantiene a Betts como líder contra los zurdos.
Anuncio
¿Podrá Betts sustentar esto en la postemporada?
Betts tiene un historial de mejorar durante los playoffs. En su primera temporada con los Dodgers, bateó .296/.378/.493 con OPS+ de 135 hasta octubre, cuando los Dodgers ganaron la Serie Mundial.
2021 fue más de lo mismo, bateando .319/.377/.404 con 116 wRC+. 2022 y 2023 terminaron temprano para los Dodgers y Betts tuvo problemas entreambos primaveras.
En 2024, cuando los Dodgers ganaron uno de sus primeros títulos consecutivos, Betts estuvo mágico, bateando .290/.387/.585 con 151 wRC+.
Durante la viejo parte de la temporada, Betts no fue lo que los fanáticos de Mookie esperaban, con un bautizo promedio de la muérdago y una gran defensa en el campocorto.
Anuncio
A partir de mediados de agosto y hasta septiembre, cambió el estandarte y dejó al manager Dave Roberts impresionado y sorprendido.
“No podría decirte que vi esto [coming]”, dijo Roberts. “Pero se ha vuelto más esforzado. Ha trabajado duro en eso… Y el hecho de que todo salga aceptablemente ha sido increíble. Simplemente no importa dónde lo golpees, a quién se enfrenta, [what’s] la situación… está tomando buenos turnos al bate”.
Betts, mientras tanto, sabía que su antigua producción a nivel de Tahúr Más Valioso todavía estaba en él.
“Sé que todavía soy capaz de hacerlo”, dijo Betts. “Sé que estaba ahí en alguna parte”.
De cara a octubre, pocos bateadores deberían hacer apreciar mejor a los fanáticos.
Su experiencia, anejo con su nueva producción, deberían ayudarlo a encajar en la fórmula, anejo con el pitcheo abridor de calidad, que lo colocará a él y a los Dodgers de 2026 en la inmortalidad de la MLB.

item.title: [Dodgers Nation] Mookie Betts' Monster September Is Setting Up a Dodgers October
item.dc:creator: Nelson Espinal
item.description: Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is having a crazy September at the plate, and he looks like someone who can carry the offense in the postseason. Betts’ Crazy September Betts is hitting .367 in September entering Friday, with 21 RBIs, six home runs, and nine doubles. item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts is having a crazy September at the plate, and he looks like someone who can carry the offense in the postseason.
Betts’ Crazy September
Betts is hitting .367 in September entering Friday, with 21 RBIs, six home runs, and nine doubles.
He has a 1.117 OPS and a 219 wRC+, both metrics highlighting just how elite he has been. It has been his best month of the season by far, and it is akin to his MVP bests.
He is walking 16% of plate appearances and striking out on just 8.5% of the time.
His approach at the plate looks great, with good swing decisions and a strong command of the strike zone that pushes pitchers to throw more challenging pitches than they would want.
When he does swing, he has 32 hard-hit balls this month, and the average exit velocity is 92.6 mph, the highest of the year thus far.
Why the Dodgers needed this production from Betts
To no one’s surprise, Betts was the team’s best hitter in September. His wRC+ is only rivaled by Josue De Paula, though his sample size was much smaller than Betts’.
Shohei Ohtani missed most of the month with a right-arm injury, while Andy Pages also missed the majority of the month, returning only in the last few days.
Additionally, Freddie Freeman and Tommy Edman have gone mostly cold, only further increasing the need for someone to step up.
Betts has been the guy to carry the offense, with 25 weighted runs created, according to FanGraphs, the most on the team, second to Teoscar Hernandez, who has 19.
With his emergence and Edman’s slump, Betts took over the leadoff spot until Ohtani returned, and his play has been so good that even after the Japanese superstar returned, manager Dave Roberts still has Betts lead off against lefties.
Can Betts keep this up in the postseason?
Betts has a track record of stepping up during the playoffs. In his first season with the Dodgers, he hit .296/.378/.493 with a 135 OPS+ through October, when the Dodgers won the World Series.
2021 was more of the same, hitting .319/.377/.404 with a 116 wRC+. 2022 and 2023 ended early for the Dodgers, and Betts struggled both years.
In 2024, when the Dodgers won one of their first consecutive titles, Betts was magical, hitting .290/.387/.585 with a 151 wRC+.
For most of the season, Betts wasn’t the Mookie fans expected, with league-average hitting and great defense at shortstop.
Starting in mid-August and into September, he flipped the script and left manager Dave Roberts impressed and surprised.
“I couldn’t tell you that I saw this [coming],” Roberts said. “But he’s got stronger. He’s worked hard on that … And just for it to come together has been great. It just doesn’t matter where you hit him, who he’s facing, [what’s] the situation –– he’s taking good at-bats.”
Betts, meanwhile, knew his former MVP-level production was still in him.
“I know I’m still capable of it,” Betts said. “I know it was in there somewhere.”
Heading into October, few hitters should make fans feel better.
His experience, along with his newfound production, should help him fit into the formula, alongside the quality starting pitching, that puts him and the 2026 Dodgers into MLB immortality.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dodgers Activate Dalton Rushing; Option Alex Freeland
item.dc:creator: Cody Snavely
item.description: SAN FRANCISCO, CA—As expected, before Game One of a three-game series against the San Francisco Giants, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated left-handed-hitting catcher Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list. In order to make room on the 28-man roster, the Dodgers optioned infielder Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City. For Rushing, these next three games are his final chance to make his case for a spot on the Dodgers’ postseason roster. Because of his UCL injury, his role will be limited t
item.content:encoded:
SAN FRANCISCO, CA—As expected, before Game One of a three-game series against the San Francisco Giants, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated left-handed-hitting catcher Dalton Rushing from the 10-day injured list.
In order to make room on the 28-man roster, the Dodgers optioned infielder Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
For Rushing, these next three games are his final chance to make his case for a spot on the Dodgers’ postseason roster. Because of his UCL injury, his role will be limited to pinch-hitting off the bench, but the second-year catcher has one last chance to show the Dodgers he can still provide an impact bat when October arrives.
This is Rushing’s second return from the injured list this month for the same injury, as the lefty lasted only eight at-bats before heading back to the IL and receiving a PRP injection to calm the pain.
In that time, while no longer on the roster due to the activation of Shohei Ohtani, the role of a left-handed hitter off the bench is also down to Josue De Paula, who posted an OPS over 1.000 and hit .323 in his short but successful stint at the major league level.
As for Alex Freeland is headed back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on September 1st. At the time, the Dodgers opted for Freeland over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling, with James Tibbs III appearing to be the expected choice for that extra position-player spot.
Instead, Freeland got the call and put together a solid month, hitting .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI across 17 games, including 10 starts. He last appeared Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
It was an inconsistent season overall for the 25-year-old, who surprisingly made the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. Freeland showed flashes at both the Major League level and with Oklahoma City, and with this move, he can rejoin the Comets for their Triple-A National Championship Game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
Unfortunately for Freeland, being optioned this late in the season also closes the door on a potential postseason roster spot. He cannot be added to the Dodgers’ National League Division Series roster in time for Game One on Saturday, October 3rd, unless he replaces a player who is placed on the injured list.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers activated Dalton Rushing off the 10-day injured list and optioned Alex Freeland to Triple-A Oklahoma City prior to Friday’s game against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland heads back to the Minors after joining the Dodgers when active rosters expanded on Sept. 1. He was chosen over an outfield prospect despite Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker both struggling at the time. James Tibbs III at one point appeared to be the expected choice for the Dodgers’ extra position player.
Instead the team elected for Freeland, who hit .250/.413/.389 with two doubles, one home run and two RBI over 17 games (10 starts) this month. Freeland last played on Saturday against the San Francisco Giants.
Freeland endured an inconsistent year after making the Dodgers’ Opening Day roster over Hyeseong Kim. He had some stretches of promise not only at the Major League level, but while with the Comets as well. The 25-year-old conceivably will join Oklahoma City for their Triple-A National Championship game in Las Vegas on Saturday.
With Freeland getting optioned this late in the season, he is not a candidate to make the Dodgers’ postseason roster for the National League Division Series. He would not be eligible to get added in time for Game 1 on Saturday, Oct. 3, unless taking the spot of an injured player.
Rushing is back from a second stint on the injured list due to trouble with his right elbow. The first instance was due to a slight tear in the UCL, but the latest came because of a flexor tendon problem.
It prompted the Dodgers to halt Rushing’s throwing progression and he now has three games to seemingly make up for lost time. Rushing had been projected to be the left-handed bat off the bench for the postseason, but Josue De Paula may now have the inside track for that role.
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts indicated Rushing would receive a maximum of three at-bats as a pinch-hitter this weekend.
Like Andy Pages and Shohei Ohtani earlier this week, Rushing is back without having gone on a rehab assignment in part because of the Minor League season ending. Though, he did log at-bats against Will Klein, who likewise is hopeful to earn a role with the Dodgers come October.

item.title: [sandiegouniontribune.com] Padres beat Dodgers to clinch third straight postseason berth
item.dc:creator: Kevin Acee
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Finally, they are in. The Padres spent sizable portions of this season seemingly on the edge of collapse every few weeks before surging back into contention. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Finally, they are in.
The Padres spent sizable portions of this season seemingly on the edge of collapse every few weeks before surging back into contention.
So being no-hit for five innings and then suddenly building a sizable lead and then holding on in a frenzied finish to the game that clinched their playoff berth seemed about right.
The Padres got their first hit and their first run in the sixth inning and scored three more times in the seventh before turning the game over to the back end of their bullpen to preserve a 4-2 victory.
Their high-leverage relievers were the strength and the most consistent part of their team all season, so it was also fitting that Jason Adam, Adrian Morejón and Mason Miller strung together the final three innings to get the Padres into the playoffs for a third consecutive season.
It is the first time in team history the Padres have qualified for three consecutive postseasons and just the 10th time they will head to the playoffs in their 58 years of existence.
This was the second time in this three-year span that the Padres were spraying champagne in the visitors’ clubhouse at Dodger Stadium, the site of so many glum postgames over the years.
The Padres had reached base just once, on a walk, in five innings against Dodgers starter Tyler Glasnow.
Then, suddenly, they took a lead with the major contributions being a single by a rookie who joined them on Sept. 1 and a sacrifice fly by a journeyman who was called up on Aug. 24.
The Padres’ first hit of the night was Ethan Salas’ flare the other way and just over the left side of the infield with one out in the sixth inning.
Fernando Tatis Jr. followed with a single grounded through the right side that sent Salas to third base, and Dustin Harris then hit a fly ball to center field that put the Padres up 1-0.
Yuki Matsui, who had gotten the final out in the fifth inning, got the first two outs in the sixth before Jason Adam threw one pitch to get the third out.
A one-out double in the seventh inning by Jackson Merrill off Glasnow and a pinch-hit single by Austin Hays after lefty Justin Wrobleski entered the game extended the Padres’ lead, and two-out singles by Salas and Tatis extended it further.
Adam retired the first two batters in the seventh. Morejón got the final out that inning and allowed a run in the eighth. Miller’s 38th save was earned with a four-out ninth inning in which the Dodgers scored again.
After Tommy Edman reached base when he swung through a slider that bounced past Salas, Shohei Ohtani doubled Edman home before Mookie Betts grounded out.
Padres starter Nick Pivetta matched Glasnow where it mattered most — on the scoreboard — for as long as he could.
He was pulled after yielding a two-out single in the fifth inning, and Matsui surrendered a single to Freddie Freeman before striking out Teoscar Hernández.
The Dodgers found out before the game that they had clinched a first-round bye in the playoffs, so they are essentially playing out the season to stay in shape.
Exactly three years after the Padres clinched a playoff berth with a victory at Dodger Stadium, they were playing on Thursday for the right to continue playing.
They are now striving over the next three days for the right to host their best-of-three National League Wild Card Series.
They are in position to do so, a game ahead of the Cubs, who also clinched a playoff berth Thursday. Because the Cubs won the series between the teams, the Padres have to finish a game ahead of the Cubs in the standings in order to remain the No.4 seed.

item.title: [DodgersBeat] Dave Roberts Mulls Changes as Dodgers Finish Home Schedule
item.dc:creator: Steve Webb
item.description: LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers will get another opportunity to secure a first-round postseason bye Thursday night, and manager Dave Roberts likes what he’s seeing from his team as October approaches. With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup, several key hitters finding their swings and Tyler Glasnow taking the mound for the final regular-season home game, the Dodgers have plenty to feel good about despite Wednesday’s loss to the Padres. Speaking with reporters before the game, Roberts discussed Ohta
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES, CA — The Dodgers will get another opportunity to secure a first-round postseason bye Thursday night, and manager Dave Roberts likes what he’s seeing from his team as October approaches. With Shohei Ohtani back in the lineup, several key hitters finding their swings and Tyler Glasnow taking the mound for the final regular-season home game, the Dodgers have plenty to feel good about despite Wednesday’s loss to the Padres.
Speaking with reporters before the game, Roberts discussed Ohtani’s encouraging return, the offensive resurgence of Kyle Tucker and Teoscar Hernández, the difficult postseason roster decisions ahead and the possibility of another meeting with San Diego in October.
One of the nuggets that Doc floated in his pregamer was the possibility of not necessarily hitting Shohei Ohtani in the leadoff spot throughou the playoffs. He might, as he did on Wednesday, use Mookie Betts in the leadoff spot on nights when the opponents throw a lefty at them.
Ohtani’s Presence Changes Everything
Roberts was asked whether a single position player can have the kind of impact in baseball that a quarterback has in football or a superstar has in basketball.
He believes Ohtani is one of the rare players capable of doing exactly that.
“Yes, he can have an impact. Certainly, the biggest impact in baseball is the starting pitcher, I believe. But as far as Shohei, what he can do in the batter’s box can certainly make that impact.”
“Every time he steps in the box, he can change the score. And when he’s in the hole, when he’s on deck, he’s always looming. That plays into the pitcher’s mind, psyche, the manager, the pitching coach.”
Roberts was particularly encouraged by Ohtani’s plate discipline Wednesday, when he went 1-for-4 with a walk and narrowly missed a home run on a seventh-inning fly ball to center field.
“I hope that’s a sign of things to come,” Roberts said. “I thought even yesterday, taking the first slider from Robbie Ray for a ball got him into a good count. Whereas the last couple weeks, just really hair-on-fire swinging and chasing. It’s a hard way to make a living that way, right?”
“I thought yesterday the patience was really good. And like I said, I hope that’s more to come.”
The manager reiterated that he wants Ohtani to control the strike zone and use the big part of the field.
“If he can do those things, then sign me up.”
As for where Ohtani will hit in the batting order going forward, Roberts is still considering his options.
“I haven’t totally decided. I’m kind of toying with it, clearly. I’m not sure exactly whether he’s going to stick in the one or rotate him depending on the pitcher. Not totally 100% yet.”
Dodgers Offense Finding Its Stride
The Dodgers managed only one run Wednesday despite collecting 10 hits, but Roberts believes the overall quality of their offensive approach has improved considerably.
Asked how he feels about the lineup compared with a month ago, particularly with Mookie Betts, Tucker and Hernández swinging the bats well, Roberts offered an enthusiastic assessment.
“I feel much better about our offense now,” he said. “We didn’t score a bunch of runs last night, but I thought how we beat the starter was a good start. And we’ve done it the last two nights.”
“It’s just a relentless lineup. You can kind of stagger them left, right, all the way one through nine. There’s no easy outs. There’s a lot of guys that can slug you. We control the strike zone.”
The simultaneous resurgence of several hitters is especially encouraging.
“Now you get Kyle getting some hits. You get Teo slugging, getting some hits, and all the while taking his walks, too.”
“This is the most we’ve had guys that are swinging the bats at the same time all year. It’s probably five guys that feel really good right now, where typically it’s one or two. So this is a good thing.”
That’s certainly a welcome development with the postseason just around the corner.
Dalton Rushing Expected Back Friday, but October Roster Remains Uncertain
Roberts confirmed that Dalton Rushing is expected to be activated Friday, although his opportunity to demonstrate his readiness for the postseason will be extremely limited.
“It’s going to be a small sample,” Roberts acknowledged. “At the most, it would be three pinch-hit at-bats. So just conduct good at-bats and see what we got.”
The manager expressed sympathy for Rushing’s difficult circumstances, particularly after dealing with multiple injuries.
“It’s just tough to be hurt, be back, then to be hurt again, and then to take three pinch-hit at-bats potentially and say, ‘Hey, you’re on the roster.'”
“But what he’s done for us this year certainly deserves some consideration. I think that’s giving him the respect and the thoughtfulness of what he’s done for us.”
Roberts also explained that the Dodgers must consider more than simply adding another left-handed bat. Bench versatility and the potential need for a pinch-runner will factor into the final decision.
“There’s also a component of having a guy that can run off the bench. So it’s not just a left-handed bat off the bench. There are some other nuanced conversations that need to happen, and what fits best for a potential first-round matchup.”
He added that a five-game Division Series creates different pitching requirements than a longer Championship Series, potentially giving the Dodgers more flexibility with their bench construction.
Glasnow Gets One More Tune-Up
Thursday’s starter, Tyler Glasnow, will make his sixth appearance since returning from the injured list.
Roberts expressed satisfaction with the right-hander’s progress, particularly his delivery and how he’s managing his outings.
“I’ve seen that he hasn’t really had concerns about the delivery. I think the ball’s coming out really well.”
“I like some of the things that he gets frustrated about versus years past. I think he’s just managing his outings really well.”
Although Roberts wants Glasnow to finish the regular season on a positive note, he emphasized that Thursday’s performance won’t determine how he views the pitcher’s postseason readiness.
“This is going to be a good one, obviously, for the confidence to go into the postseason. But either way, it’s not make or break. I just want him to pitch well and feel good going into October.”
A Potential October Preview
Roberts acknowledged that the Dodgers are paying close attention to the Padres during this final regular-season series, recognizing that the two clubs could meet again in the playoffs.
He mentioned gathering information on Robbie Ray, Michael King and San Diego’s bullpen, with Nick Pivetta scheduled to pitch Thursday.
The Dodgers are also keeping an eye on the Braves, whose result against Cincinnati could affect Los Angeles’ opportunity to clinch the bye.
But Roberts said a favorable result on the out-of-town scoreboard wouldn’t change his approach in the middle of Thursday’s game.
“We’re playing to win, and I don’t think if the scoreboard reads that they’re winning or they lost, it would change anything.”
“I want to win tonight.”
Four Million Reasons to Celebrate Dodger Baseball
Thursday’s home finale also comes with a significant milestone, as the Dodgers are expected to surpass four million in attendance for the second consecutive season.
Roberts praised the organization’s ability to draw fans from around the world and the atmosphere they create at Dodger Stadium.
“The amazing thing is that it’s not just localized, clearly. It’s not just domestic. It’s international. You look at everyone, everyone looks different in Dodger Stadium. It’s spectacular, and our players certainly feed off of it.”
“It’s not taken for granted. I think opponents feel it, certainly in the later innings, when they see the third deck full and the speakers are blaring.”
Roberts credited the organization’s ownership and front office for consistently putting a star-studded team on the field.
“Los Angeles loves stars, and they want to see superstars, and we have a lot of superstars, which draws people. And I think our product is very consistent.”
For a team preparing for its 14th consecutive postseason appearance, Thursday offers another opportunity to reward those fans with something worth celebrating.
The Dodgers have already clinched the NL West. Now they can secure the first-round bye, give their pitching staff some much-needed rest and head into October with their biggest stars appearing to find their form at precisely the right time.
More Dodgers Coverage:
Have you subscribed to the Bleed Los Podcast YouTube channel? Be sure to ring the notification bell to watch player interviews, participate in shows & promotions, and stay up to date on all Dodgers news and rumors!
A lifelong baseball fan, Webb has been going to Dodger games since he moved to Los Angeles in 1987. His favorite memory was attending the insane Game 3 of the World Series in 2025 and hugging random Dodgers fans after Freddie’s walkoff homer. He has been writing for Dodgersbeat since 2020.

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers and San Diego Padres are facing off in the rubber match of their three-game series on Thursday night with plenty at stake for both teams.
The Dodgers, who have already won the National League West division, can clinch a first-round bye with a win or Atlanta Braves loss over the season's final four games.
They're also still chasing the Milwaukee Brewers for the No. 1 seed, but will need some help to secure home-field advantage throughout the postseason.
As for the Padres, they're looking to clinch a postseason spot, with their magic number currently sitting at 1.
Thus, the winner of Thursday's game will be celebrating in some capacity. If it's the Padres, they'll be making a champagne and beer mess in the visitor's clubhouse at Dodger Stadium. If it's the Dodgers, they'll be shaking hands and looking forward to their five-day layoff beginning next week.
Dodgers vs Padres Pitching Matchup on Thursday
Right-handed pitcher Tyler Glasnow is taking the mound for the Dodgers in his final tune-up before the postseason.
Glasnow has been shaky since coming off the injured list at the end of August, sporting a 4.50 ERA over 28 innings with 38 strikeouts to 10 walks. Overall this season, he's 5-1 with a 3.46 ERA and 87 strikeouts across 67.2 innings (12 starts).
Glasnow is expected to be the team's No. 4 starter in the playoffs behind Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal and Blake Snell.
Opposite Glasnow will be Padres right-hander Nick Pivetta, who missed nearly five months this season with an elbow injury but has been incredibly sharp since returning.
In his three starts since coming off the IL, Pivetta has allowed just three runs over 14 innings for a 1.93 ERA. He has 11 strikeouts to one walk in that time.
Dodgers Starting Lineup
- Shohei Ohtani, DH
- Mookie Betts, SS
- Freddie Freeman, 1B
- Teoscar Hernández, LF
- Kyle Tucker, RF
- Max Muncy, 3B
- Andy Pages, CF
- Hunter Feduccia, C
- Tommy Edman, 2B
How to Watch Dodgers vs Padres on Thursday
First pitch for Los Angeles Dodgers vs. San Diego Padres on Thursday, Sept. 24 is 7:10 p.m. PT/10:10 p.m. ET.
The game will be broadcast on SportsNet LA and in the MLB app.
The game will be broadcast on the radio on AM570 (in English) and KTNQ 1020 AM (in Spanish).
