item.content:encoded:
Field Level Media

24 Sep 2026, 13:49 GMT+10

(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres moved to the brink of their third consecutive playoff appearance with a 5-1 road victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday.
Fernando Tatis Jr. had three hits as the Padres reduced their magic number for clinching a National League wild-card spot to one. San Diego sits in the top NL wild-card position, one game ahead of both the Chicago Cubs and the Philadelphia Phillies.
San Diego won for the 14th time in its past 16 games while coming out on top for just the fourth time in 12 games against Los Angeles this season. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
In his return to the roster after recovering from knee and biceps injuries, Shohei Ohtani went 1-for-4 with a walk as the Dodgers saw their 11-game home winning streak end. Andy Pages and Teoscar Hernandez each had three hits while Los Angeles ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9) gave up four runs (two earned) on five hits over six innings.
Brewers 4, Phillies 1
Brice Turang and Christian Yelich hit early home runs as visiting Milwaukee topped Philadelphia.
William Contreras knocked in two runs for the Brewers, who extended their franchise-record win total. Milwaukee needs to capture one of its final four games to reach 100 victories for the first time in team history. Logan Henderson (11-3) allowed one run in five innings.
Philadelphia starter Aaron Nola (7-11) permitted four runs and four hits in six innings. Bryson Stott doubled twice for the Phillies, who have a magic number of two to clinch a playoff berth.
Marlins 3, Cubs 2
Esteury Ruiz's hustle enabled visiting Miami to score the go-ahead run in the seventh inning, leading to a win over Chicago.
After a video review, Ruiz was declared safe at second base on what was originally ruled an inning-ending double play, with Agustin Ramirez scoring to break a 2-2 tie. Cade Gibson (6-2) threw one perfect inning, and ace Sandy Alcantara recorded his second save.
Cubs starter Kevin Gausman allowed two runs in 5 2/3 innings, exiting after hurting his left shoulder while diving to make a tag at third base. Dansby Swanson hit a two-run single in the bottom of the sixth after Kyle Stowers socked a two-run homer in the top of the frame.
Diamondbacks 5, Rockies 3
Tim Tawa homered, Gabriel Moreno had three hits and Arizona continued its drive for a postseason berth with a win over Colorado in Denver.
The Diamondbacks have won four straight to move within three games of the Phillies and the Cubs in the chase for the last two NL wild-card positions with four games to play. Arizona starter Merrill Kelly (10-14) allowed two runs on four hits in 5 1/3 innings.
Ezequiel Tovar homered and finished with two hits for the Rockies, who lost for the 14th time in 16 games. Rookie Mason Adams (0-2) struck out a career-high eight over a career-best six innings. He yielded four runs, all unearned, on five hits.
Mariners 6, Astros 5 (10 innings)
Josh Naylor lined a one-out single to center field with the bases loaded in the bottom of the 10th inning to score the deciding run as Seattle kept its slim playoff hopes alive with a victory against visiting Houston.
Dominic Canzone drove in three runs for the Mariners, whose only chance to make the postseason is to finish in a three-way tie with Houston and Texas, who are tied atop the American League West. Julio Rodriguez's bases-loaded walk tied the game before Naylor's winning hit.
Yainer Diaz hit a tiebreaking triple in the top of the 10th inning after earlier belting a two-run homer for the Astros. Houston closer Josh Hader (4-2) took the loss.
Mets 7, Rangers 2
Marcus Semien damaged his former team's playoff hopes when he hit a tiebreaking solo homer in the eighth inning to help New York prevail in Arlington, Texas.
Juan Soto socked a two-run homer in the third and Brett Baty added insurance with a pinch-hit grand slam in the ninth for the Mets. New York starter Nolan McLean (12-10) gave up two runs in seven innings.
The Rangers managed just four hits while losing their third game in a row. Jacob Latz (3-4) served up Semien's homer.
Red Sox 1, Guardians 0
Andruw Monasterio's sixth-inning RBI single and Sonny Gray's six shutout innings propelled Boston past visiting Cleveland.
The Red Sox managed the lone run on 12 hits, all singles. They went 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position and left eight men on base through five innings before Monasterio's run-scoring single broke the deadlock. Gray (18-5), who allowed four hits, increased his AL-leading win total.
Cleveland starter Foster Griffin (15-6) worked six frames, allowing one run on 10 hits. The Guardians remained tied with the White Sox atop the AL Central.
Royals 5, White Sox 4
Maikel Garcia's tiebreaking double in the seventh inning capped a three-hit, three-RBI night as Kansas City beat visiting Chicago.
While the Royals snapped a five-game skid, the White Sox missed a chance to regain control of the AL Central and clinch a playoff berth.
Connor Thomas (2-1) tossed two shutout innings for the win, and Steven Cruz recorded his eighth save. Kansas City's Carter Jensen and Chicago's Braden Montgomery each had three hits and a run.
Braves 3, Reds 2 (10 innings)
Mauricio Dubon's infield chopper to the mound in the 10th inning gave host Atlanta a walk-off victory over Cincinnati.
Braves starter Chris Sale pitched 5 2/3 innings and allowed one run while striking out 10, reaching 200 strikeouts for the ninth time in his career. Matt Olson and Austin Riley homered for Atlanta, and Brent Suter (3-2) tossed a perfect top of the 10th.
Juan Brito led off the game with a home run, and he and Matt McLain each had two hits for the Reds. Cincinnati starter Andrew Abbott fired a season-high seven innings and allowed two runs.
Orioles 4, Blue Jays 2 (Game 1)
Baltimore's Pete Alonso hit another home run and the Orioles eliminated visiting Toronto from playoff contention by winning in the first game of a doubleheader.
The Blue Jays were the reigning American League champions, but they won't have a chance to return to the World Series.
Chris Bassitt (9-5) pitched five-plus innings to notch a victory in his third consecutive start. He gave up two runs on seven hits. Max Scherzer (3-9) surrendered four runs and four hits in five innings.
Orioles 4, Blue Jays 2 (Game 2)
Christian Encarnacion-Strand homered and drove in three runs and Trey Gibson took a shutout into the seventh inning as Baltimore completed a doubleheader sweep of visiting Toronto to stay in playoff contention.
Baltimore must win its remaining three games and have the White Sox lose their remaining four in order to have a chance for an AL wild-card spot. Gibson (2-3), a rookie who hadn't pitched in the major leagues since June 30, gave up three hits in 6 2/3 innings.
Davis Schneider hit a two-run ninth-inning homer off Felix Bautista in the nightcap for the Blue Jays. Toronto rookie starter CJ Van Eyk (0-2) allowed four runs on four hits in five innings.
Yankees 9, Rays 2
Ryan McMahon hit a third-inning grand slam and tied a career high with five RBIs while Ben Rice hit a pair of solo homers as host New York rolled past Tampa Bay.
McMahon drove in five runs for the fourth time in his career. Rice homered on the first pitch of the contest to become the 13th Yankee with 40 homers in a season. He later hit his 41st. Gerrit Cole (10-9) allowed two runs on three hits in 5 2/3 innings.
Jonny DeLuca hit an RBI double and Cedric Mullins homered for the Rays. Mason Englert (0-4) allowed eight runs on nine hits over 3 2/3 innings.
Nationals 4, Tigers 2
Yohandy Morales hit a two-run homer and visiting Washington held on for a victory over Detroit as the Nationals won the three-game series 2-1.
Brady House had two hits and scored a run while CJ Abrams, who homered twice on Tuesday, reached base three times and knocked in a run for Washington. Will Dion (2-2) tossed two innings of one-run relief, and Yovanny Cruz got four outs for his first career save.
Detroit starter Framber Valdez (10-12) gave up two runs and four hits over 5 1/3 innings. Ben Malgeri homered and drove in both of the Tigers' runs, and Kevin McGonigle added three hits.
Twins 4, Giants 2
Pinch hitter Walker Jenkins broke a seventh-inning tie with an RBI single as Minnesota completed a 4-3 road trip with a win over San Francisco.
Luke Keaschall drove in two runs with a homer and a sacrifice fly while Josh Bell added an RBI single for the Twins. Yoendrys Gomez (3-4) threw 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief, and Andrew Morris escaped a ninth-inning jam for his fifth save.
Shay Whitcomb had two hits for the Giants, who have lost five out of six. Reliever Dylan Smith (0-6) yielded two runs while getting just two outs.
Cardinals 5, Pirates 1
Matthew Liberatore struck out six over 5 2/3 innings and JJ Wetherholt had three hits and an RBI to lead St. Louis to a victory at Pittsburgh.
Liberatore (6-14) allowed only one run -- on a solo homer by Brandon Lowe -- as the Cardinals snapped the Pirates' season-high-tying five-game winning streak. St. Louis' Jose Fermin went 2-for-4.
Lowe had two hits and Ryan O'Hearn added two doubles for Pittsburgh. Pirates reliever Brandon Eisert (3-3) gave up three runs in two-thirds of an inning.
Athletics 7, Angels 3
Rookie Henry Bolte recorded the first four-hit game of his career and Donovan Walton hit a three-run homer to help the Athletics top Los Angeles in West Sacramento, Calif.
Shea Langeliers had a two-run double and Bolte scored twice, had two doubles and drove in one run for the A's, who assured they will avoid a 100-loss season. Geoff Hartlieb (2-1) threw 1 2/3 innings of scoreless relief.
Mike Trout and Vaughn Grissom homered for the Angels, who are two losses shy of the first 100-loss season in franchise history. Walbert Urena (9-11) allowed five runs and seven hits over four innings.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
After shutting out the Padres on Tuesday, the Dodgers could only muster one run in a 5-1 defeat on Wednesday, snapping their home winning streak at 11 games.
Dodgers 11-game home winning streak snapped in 5-1 loss to Padres
Yoshinobu Yamamoto tallies six innings but gets one run of support, Manny Machado’s home run makes the difference.
Both Yoshinobu Yamamoto and Robbie Ray kept the hitters in check over their first three innings, as Yamamoto secured three shutout innings on just 36 pitches while Ray needed 70 pitches in that same time.
Yamamoto began the top of the fourth inning by brushing the jersey of Dustin Harris on an inside pitch to give San Diego a leadoff baserunner, and Manny Machado ensured the Padres wouldn’t be shut out again as he launched a two-run home run to center field to give San Diego the first lead.
The Dodgers responded with two consecutive singles from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker to begin the bottom of the fourth inning, and Andy Pages had his first hit back from the injured list with a bloop single to center field. Ray managed to get Max Muncy to fly out to shallow center, but his night was done after tossing 84 pitches over 3 1/3 innings. He was charged with a run as Tommy Edman lifted a sacrifice fly to put the Dodgers on the board. Mookie Betts walked on four pitches to make it bases loaded with two outs for Shohei Ohtani, but David Morgan got him whiffing on a fastball at 99 miles per hour on a 3-2 count to leave them loaded.
San Diego picked up where they left off against Yamamoto in the top of the fifth inning, as Ethan Salas and Fernando Tatis Jr. both singled to open the frame. A bunt attempt from Harris was hit right back to Yamamoto, but an errant throw to third allowed Salas to score. Manny Machado brought home Tatis with a sacrifice fly to center field, giving him three RBI on the night and making it a three-run San Diego lead.
Yamamoto would finish his night going six innings, marking the first time he didn’t log at least seven innings in the month of September. Wednesday’s outing was the first time since September 2 where Yamamoto allowed at least two earned runs, with his four strikeouts on the night being the fewest since he struck out three against the Boston Red Sox on August 1. Yamamoto ends the regular season with a 2.53 ERA, striking out 182 hitters across 185 innings.
The Dodger bullpen would hold San Diego in check until the top of the ninth inning as Blake Treinen allowed an RBI single to Freddy Fermin, allowing Samad Taylor to score to make it a 5-1 Padres lead.
Teoscar Hernández recorded another three-hit game, his third of the month, finishing 3-4 with three singles while raising his season average to .270 for the first time since June 30.
Andy Pages also finished with a three-hit night in his second game off the injured list, giving him his first multi-hit game since August 17 against the Colorado Rockies. Shohei Ohtani finished 1-4 with a single, a walk and two strikeouts in his first game off the injured list.
With the Dodgers losing on Wednesday, they once again sit two games back of the Milwaukee Brewers for the top seed in the National League playoff picture. The Dodgers are still four games above the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye, and their magic number to secure a bye remains at 1.
Game particulars
- Home runs— Manny Machado (29)
- WP— Yuki Matsui (4-1): 1 IP, 1 hit, 0 runs, 1 walk, 0 strikeouts
- LP— Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9): 6 IP, 5 hits, 4 runs (2 earned runs), 1 walk, 4 strikeouts
Up next
The Dodgers play their final home game of the regular season against San Diego on Thursday (7:10 p.m. PT, SportsNet LA) before heading up to San Francisco for their final regular season series. Tyler Glasnow faces Nick Pivetta.

item.content:encoded:
Padres down Dodgers, grab solo lead in NL wild-card standings
(Photo credit: Jayne Kamin)
Manny Machado homered and drove in three runs as the San Diego Padres moved to the brink of their third consecutive playoff appearance with a 5-1 road victory over the Los Angeles Dodgers on Wednesday.
Fernando Tatis Jr. had three hits as the Padres (88-70) reduced their magic number for clinching a National League wild-card spot to one. San Diego sits in the top NL wild-card position, one game ahead of both the Chicago Cubs (87-71) and the Philadelphia Phillies (87-71).
Five San Diego relievers combined for 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Bradgley Rodriguez (4-3) fanned three in two innings.
San Diego won for the 14th time in its past 16 games while coming out on top for just the fourth time in 12 games against Los Angeles this season. The Padres have never reached the playoffs in three consecutive seasons.
In his return to the active roster after recovering from knee and biceps injuries, Shohei Ohtani went 1-for-4 with a walk as the Dodgers (97-61) saw their 11-game home winning streak end. Ohtani struck out with the bases loaded to end the fourth inning and flied out to the wall in center field in the seventh.
Andy Pages and Teoscar Hernandez each had three hits while Los Angeles ace Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-9) gave up four runs (two earned) on five hits over six innings but was burned by his own throwing error. Yamamoto fanned four and walked one.
Machado gave the Padres a 2-0 lead in the fourth when he crushed a first-pitch sinker from Yamamoto over the center field wall for his 29th home run of the season.
The Dodgers loaded the bases with no outs in the bottom of the fourth. Robbie Ray got Max Muncy to fly out, then was replaced by David Morgan after 3 1/3 innings. Morgan gave up a sacrifice fly to Edman, cutting the Padres' lead to 2-1, before striking out Ohtani.
Ohtani appeared to walk on a 3-1 pitch, but Padres catcher Ethan Salas successfully challenged the pitch. Morgan eventually got Ohtani swinging at a 3-2 sinker.
The Padres made it 3-1 in the fifth when Yamamoto was off target on a throw to third base following a bunt from Dustin Harris with runners on first and second. Salas scored on the play, and Machado followed with a sacrifice fly to right-center for a 4-1 lead.
San Diego added a run in the ninth. Samad Taylor walked, stole second and third and came home on a single from Freddy Fermin.
--Field Level Media

item.content:encoded:
As expected, the Los Angeles Dodgers activated Shohei Ohtani from the injured list on Wednesday. In a corresponding move, they demoted a player who turned out to be a more capable replacement than anyone could've imagined for two weeks.
That would be rookie slugger Josue De Paula, who was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City, a team whose season could end as soon as Wednesday. De Paula, the top prospect in the Dodgers' system and one of the best overall prospects in baseball, was promoted to replace Ohtani on the roster.
Ohtani will hit second in his first game back against the San Diego Padres, marking his first time not batting leadoff for the Dodgers since June 16, 2024. The red-hot Mookie Betts is filling the leadoff spot instead against Padres left-hander Robbie Ray.
De Paula, meanwhile, will be making his Triple-A debut as a starter for the Oklahoma City Comets in Game 2 of the PCL championship series.
In the 11 games Ohtani missed, no player on the Dodgers reached base more than De Paula. The Dodgers went 11-3 in that span and clinched both a playoff berth and the NL West while moving into strong position to secure a wild-card bye.
Between his cameo in L.A. and a performance in Double-A that won him Texas League MVP honors at 21 years old, De Paula has inspired questions about a place on the Dodgers' postseason roster.
As The Athletic's Katie Woo points out, De Paula being optioned on Wednesday means he will be eligible to be recalled by Oct. 3, when the Dodgers will begin playing the NLDS. He isn't technically eligible for the playoffs because he wasn't on the Los Angeles 40-man roster on Sept. 1, but that can be remedied by petitioning the commissioner's office for him to replace a player going on the injured list.
With Ohtani taking up the designated hitter spot and corner outfielders Teoscar Hernandez and Kyle Tucker both resurrecting down seasons over the past month or so, there's not a natural place for De Paula in the starting lineup.
Per The Athletic, De Paula is still in the mix for a postseason roster spot but appears to be in competition with Dalton Rushing for the role of premium left-handed bench bat. Rushing has been attempting to play through a partially torn UCL since early August. He won't be playing his usual catcher position again in 2026, but he could still hit.
Rushing is expected to be activated sometime this week, at which point he too will be trying to justify October at-bats in the final games of the regular season. De Paula has set a high bar to clear in that regard.
Figuring out where to put a rising star because your superstar is healthy again is ultimately a good problem to have. Whoever is on the roster, the Dodgers are on track to play the Atlanta Braves or Padres in the NLDS, though that could still change in the coming days.

item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — The Dodgers on Wednesday activated Shohei Ohtani off the injured list on his first day eligible to return after the minimum 15 days on the sideline with right biceps inflammation. Josue De Paula was optioned to Triple-A Oklahoma City.
The plan is for Ohtani to be the designated hitter for the remaining five games of the regular season, to get him back in the swing of things at the plate. An accumulation of injuries ate into a very productive season for the four-time MVP. Left knee inflammation prevented Ohtani from pitching after July 3, and the right biceps injury started showing signs at the plate as well.
Ohtani last homered on August 18, part of a stretch of three home runs in two days at Coors Field. On that date, Ohtani was hitting .294/.390/.558 with a 153 wRC+, leading the National League in slugging percentage and OPS, and a close second to Pete Crow-Armstrong (155) in wRC+.
But in 13 games since, Ohtani had just six hits in 49 at-bats (.122/.295/.184) with 21 strikeouts and 10 walks. The Dodgers tried avoiding the IL, giving Ohtani four days off before returning on September 7, when he was hitless in three at-bats plus a walk, but aggravated the right biceps injury on a swing. That was the last straw that finally landed Ohtani on the injured list for extended rest.
“When he’s activated, he’s going to be in the best physical place he’s been in quite some time,” manager Dave Roberts said over the weekend, than on Tuesday added, “I would say if he was a five, he’s probably an eight or nine right now.”
Ohtani on the shelf opened a door for De Paula, the Dodgers’ top prospect, to get called up directly from Double-A. The Dodgers were hesitant to give De Paula playing time in the corner outfield, sticking with Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker, who have each thrived in September. But with designated hitter open, De Paula had a chance to play every day, and he seized the opportunity.
De Paula has reached base in half of his 42 plate appearances, hitting .323/.500/.581 with three doubles, a triple, and a home run in his 11 games, and he has 11 walks against only five strikeouts.
“I think Josue has done a fantastic job,” Roberts said Tuesday.
Sending De Paula down to the minors means he won’t play in any of the Dodgers’ final five regular season games, but it doesn’t prevent him from making the postseason roster. De Paula needs to be on optional assignment for at least 10 days, a clock that does not stop for teams in the postseason. Getting sent down on Wednesday means his first day eligible to return is Saturday, October 3, which is the day of Game 1 of the National League Division Series.
He’s in a battle with Dalton Rushing for the left-handed bat off the bench, and De Paula has the built-in advantages that Rushing can’t really play in the field with the partially torn UCL in his right elbow, and that Rushing has been sidelined for two and a half weeks on the injured list.
“To be quite frank, it’s going to be tougher for Dalton given the time he’s missed, and to think that you have [three] games to get back into playoff form, it’s tough to do,” Roberts said Tuesday. “It’s not a knock on him, he’s been great for us, but it’s still tough, right, Given that we talk about having the consistency of at-bats recently from Josue. But we have to have those conversations and make a decision.”

item.title: [si.com] Padres vs. Dodgers Prediction, Odds, Probable Pitchers, Prop Bets for Wednesday, Sept. 23
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gilbert

item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers host the San Diego Padres in the middle game of their three-game set on Wednesday night.
The Dodgers opened the series with a 7-0 victory last night to extend their winning streak to five games. They are now one game back of the Brewers for the best record in the National League, and should be getting Shohei Ohtani back tonight.
That loss ended a five-game winning streak for the Padres, who are now in a three-way tie in the NL Wild Card race.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] How Can Dodgers Legally Get Josue De Paula On Postseason Roster?
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula. That has not seemed to bother De Paula, who has a 1.081 OPS in 11 games with 11 walks and just five strikeouts. De Paula has gotten to serve as the designated hi
item.content:encoded:
In an unprecedented move in the Andrew Friedman era, the Los Angeles Dodgers called up a position player directly from Double-A earlier this month: Josue De Paula.
De Paula is not a good defender, but his bat is off the charts. He has a great eye at the plate and dominated in Double-A. Still, the big leagues are a whole different thing. That has not seemed to bother De Paula, who has a 1.081 OPS in 11 games with 11 walks and just five strikeouts.
De Paula has gotten to serve as the designated hitter with Shohei Ohtani out, but that's about to change. His defense is not good enough to start in left field, and the Dodgers are not going to start him over Andy Pages, Teoscar Hernández or Kyle Tucker right now. However, he would still be a very valuable bat for the postseason, with the ability to get on base at a high clip.
There's one big problem, however. He was not on the 40-man roster on Sept. 1, which is the eligibility cutoff for the postseason. The Dodgers can still legally get De Paula on a postseason roster, but will need to petition the commissioner's office.
"A player who doesn't meet said criteria for postseason eligibility can still be added to a team's roster in the postseason via petition to the Commissioner's Office if the player was in the organization on Aug. 31 and is replacing someone who is on the injured list and has served the minimum amount of time required for activation," read Major League Baseball's rules for postseason eligibility. "(For example, a player on the 10-day injured list who has been on it for at least 10 days, or a player who has been on the 60-day injured list for at least 60 days.) Players who are acquired in September or after are ineligible."
De Paula is good on the first need, but the Dodgers would have to say he's replacing Dalton Rushing, who is the only current Dodger who has exceeded a minimum stay on the injured list. This would make sense, as Rushing may not be able to catch anyway and would be used as a pinch hitter. De Paula can fill that role.
More MLB: Dodgers' Freddie Freeman Explains Why Dodgers Need Bye This Year

item.title: [ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos] Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
item.source: ABC News - Breaking News, Latest News and Videos
item.dc:creator: ABC News; BETH HARRIS AP sports writer
item.description: Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best recor
item.content:encoded:
Dodgers score 5 two-out runs off Padres starter Michael King in 7-0 victory
Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month
LOS ANGELES -- Tommy Edman and Will Smith homered as the Los Angeles Dodgers scored six runs with two outs to beat the San Diego Padres 7-0 on Tuesday night in a series opener between rivals with the two best records in the majors this month.
The Dodgers (97-60) moved within one game of NL Central champion Milwaukee (98-59) for the top mark in the big leagues and home-field advantage throughout the postseason. However, the Brewers own the head-to-head tiebreaker.
Los Angeles needs one win or an Atlanta loss to clinch a first-round bye into a National League Division Series.
The NL West champion Dodgers improved to 15-5 in September with their fifth straight victory; the Padres fell to 14-5 and had their five-game winning streak snapped.
San Diego is tied with Chicago and Philadelphia at 87-70 for the three NL wild cards — four games ahead of Arizona with five to play.
Fernando Tatis Jr. and Manny Machado were a combined 1 for 7 with five strikeouts for the Padres.
The Dodgers chased Michael King (12-10) after four innings in his career-high 32nd start of the season. The right-hander gave up five runs on six hits and struck out five as his four-game winning streak ended.
Los Angeles broke out with four runs in the second. King got the first two outs on six pitches before loading the bases. Teoscar Hernández and rookie Josue De Paula hit consecutive singles before King plunked Andy Pages, who just came off the injured list.
King then issued back-to-back walks to Edman and Mookie Betts, forcing in two runs. Freddie Freeman's two-run single made it 4-0.
Betts had a ground-rule double and scored on Freeman's two-out single for a 5-0 lead in the fourth.
Edman's solo shot came with two outs in the sixth and Smith added a 396-foot drive with one out in the seventh for a 7-0 lead.
Brock Stewart started a bullpen game and Justin Wrobleski (12-5) got the win for the Dodgers, who used eight pitchers to earn the fifth shutout in franchise history when deploying at least that many.
Among them was reliever Edwin Díaz, who struck out two in one inning. Roki Sasaki's four-seam fastball touched 100 mph while he pitched one inning. The Japanese right-hander came off the injured list earlier Tuesday after missing nearly a month with a blister on his right middle finger.
Padres LHP Robbie Ray (13-8, 3.60 ERA) starts Wednesday against Dodgers RHP Yoshinobu Yamamoto (14-8, 2.51).
___
This story has been corrected to show the Dodgers scored six runs with two outs, not five.
___

item.title: [True Blue LA] Dodgers rout Padres in bulk in opener
item.dc:creator: Eric Stephen
item.description: LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium. With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular seaso
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — On a night the Los Angeles Queens won a championship in the inaugural season of the Women’s Pro Baseball League, the Los Angeles Dodgers beat a King. Four runs with two outs in the second inning off Michael King paced a 7-0 win for the Dodgers over the San Diego Padres in Tuesday night’s series opener at Dodger Stadium.
With the win, the Dodgers are up five games on the Atlanta Braves for the No. 2 seed in the National League playoffs, with five games remaining in the regular season. The Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a bye into the NLDS is down to just one.
King hadn’t allowed more than three runs in any of his previous nine starts, with a 2.26 ERA during that span, and he retired his first five batters faced on Tuesday. Then with two outs in the second inning, the next six batters reached, breaking open the scoring.
Teoscar Hernández singles for the Dodgers’ first hit, then Josue De Paula singled on an 0-2 pitch before Andy Pages was hit by a pitch in his very first plate appearance back since getting hit by a pitch one month prior, to load the bases. Tommy Edman walked on four pitches for the game’s first run, Mookie Betts only needed five pitches to walk home another run, then Freddie Freeman grounded a single through the infield, and under the legs of a leaping Edman, to score two more.
Betts hit a ground-rule double in the fourth, followed by another RBI single by Freeman for a fifth run against King.
Solo home runs by Edman in the sixth and Will Smith in the seventh off the Padres bullpen padded the scoring.
With Emmet Sheehan optioned on Tuesday and Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list, the Dodgers have only three active pitchers they plan to use as starting pitchers in the postseason at the moment. That means they have 11 relievers, and on a day following an off day and the day before a start by the MLB leader in innings per start, the Dodgers used .. pitchers to cover the nine innings.
Starters Justin Wrobleski and Roki Sasaki — the latter just activated on Tuesday — each pitched only one inning, both scoreless. Sasaki was hitting 100 mph in his first game action in four weeks.
Kyle Hurt was the only Dodgers pitcher to toss more than one inning, taking care of the sixth and seventh.
Jack Dreyer was the first pitcher of Sunday’s game, and the last pitcher on Tuesday.
It’s only the third time in franchise history the Dodgers used eight pitchers in a shutout of no more than nine innings, done also on September 29, 2019 in San Francisco and May 15 this year in Anaheim. For some perspective, when the Dodgers beat the Expos 1-0 Montreal in 22 innings on August 23, 1989 — Rick Dempsey homered, Tommy Lasorda got Expos mascot Youppi ejected — the Dodgers only used five pitchers that day.
Tuesday particulars
Home runs: Tommy Edman (8), Will Smith (10)
WP — Justin Wrobleski (12-5): 1 IP, 1 hit
LP — Michael King (12-10): 4 IP, 6 hits, 5 runs, 2 walks, 5 strikeouts

Will Smith, C 4. Max Muncy, 3B 5. Kyle Tucker, RF 6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF 7. Josue De Paula, DH 8. Andy Pages, CF 9. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers are opening up for a blockbuster series, their last big test, against the San Diego Padres.
Dodgers Lineup
1. Mookie Betts, SS
2. Freddie Freeman, 1B
3. Will Smith, C
4. Max Muncy, 3B
5. Kyle Tucker, RF
6. Teoscar Hernandez, LF
7. Josue De Paula, DH
8. Andy Pages, CF
9. Tommy Edman, 2B
Andy Pages is back in the batting order after being activated from the injured list. He broke his hand after getting hit by a pitch, had surgery, and after a month on the shelf, he is back.
It may take some time for him to shake off the rust at the plate, but his defense should not skip a beat.
The Dodgers are facing righty Michael King, but many of the hottest bats are righties.
Mookie Betts, Will Smith, and Kyle Tucker are among the most dialed-in hitters, and they should drive most of the offense.
Ideally, Freddie Freeman gets going again, since he hasn’t looked right in a while.
Who’s pitching for the Dodgers
The Dodgers will have Brock Stewart as the opener, with Roki Sasaki getting the bulk of the work out of the bullpen.
On Tuesday, hours before the game, Sasaki was activated off the injured list after recovering from his blister.
Sasaki has been great since the All-Star break, posting a 3.05 ERA with 37 strikeouts and 15 walks.
His splitter and slider are fantastic, while the fastball has been the difference-maker, showing some renewed life.
The Japanese righty is set to enter the bullpen in a varied role, either stepping in for a struggling starter or pitching late in high-leverage spots.
Stewart, meanwhile, has been a bit lucky, with a 2.55 ERA and a 3.91 FIP.
FanGraphs’ pitching models have appreciated his stuff and command, and while he has pitched better lately, he is prone to giving up hard contact.

item.title: [marinij.com] Wilkinson’s impressive five shutout innings can’t prevent SF Giants from being swept by Dodgers
item.dc:creator: Justice delos Santos
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever. Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts. “Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swe
item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Matt Wilkinson’s role has been nebulous during his short time in the majors. In his debut, he was an opener. On some days, he’s made traditional starts. In others, he’s been a multi-inning reliever.
Wilkinson is one of several young, inexperienced pitchers on this roster trying to prove he can start at the major-league level. His performance on Sunday afternoon at Dodger Stadium helped those efforts.
“Tugboat” couldn’t prevent the Giants, who lost 3-1 to the Dodgers, from being swept, but the rookie turned in arguably the best start of his short career. In his seventh career appearance, Wilkinson tossed five shutout innings against the NL West champions, collecting a career-high six strikeouts without recording a single walk.
“He was outstanding,” said manager Tony Vitello. “Back at it on the starting deal. To be honest with you, didn’t have a whole lot of trouble to navigate because of how well he threw the ball. … When there was potential for things brewing, he put an end to it.”
“Best one yet since being up,” Wilkinson said. “Really was just throwing all four pitches for strikes today, and that was kind of the mindset going into today. Compete with all four pitches, and I felt like I did a good job with that today.”
Vitello said it’s “too early” to know how Wilkinson could fit into next year’s pitching plans but assessed that Wilkinson is “pretty flexible.” Before Sunday, Wilkinson had pitched five scoreless innings with four strikeouts over his last two outings as a multi-inning reliever. When asked if he prefers starting or relieving, the 23-year-old responded he’s willing to pitch whatever role is needed.
“You want a guy that wants the ball and ain’t scared of those situations,” Vitello said.
Wilkinson certainly didn’t look scared in his first meeting with the reigning back-to-back World Series champions on their home turf. Even with Shohei Ohtani on the injured list and Kyle Tucker starting the day on the bench, the Dodgers’ lineup still featured future Hall of Famers Mookie Betts and Freddie Freeman and multi-time All-Stars Max Muncy and Teoscar Hernández.
Against Wilkinson, that group couldn’t get anything cooking.
The only threats that the Dodgers posed against Wilkinson were one-out doubles in the second and fifth innings. On both occasions, Wilkinson maneuvered out of trouble and completed five innings for just the second time in his career.
“Especially with this rivalry, it’s awesome and fun to be a small piece of that,” Wilkinson said.
Despite Wilkinson’s efforts, the Dodgers generated enough offense after his departure to complete the dusting.
Tommy Edman tied the game in the bottom of the sixth by turning a 2-2 cutter from Carson Seymour into a solo homer, and Kiké Hernández drove in the go-ahead run in the bottom of the seventh. Muncy, a long-time Giants (64-92) foe, added an RBI single in the bottom of the eighth for insurance.
Jonah Cox, with the use of his elite speed, generated San Francisco’s lone run in the top of the first.
Cox began the afternoon with a leadoff walk, then scrambled to second when the Dodgers’ Jack Dreyer made an errant pickoff throw. Already in scoring position, Cox swiped third with ease, his 14th steal of the season, then scored on a single by Victor Bericoto.
Following Dreyer’s lone inning as the opener, San Francisco couldn’t generate any offense against Los Angeles’ Emmet Sheehan, who allowed one hit over 5 1/3 scoreless innings of long relief with nine strikeouts. Sheehan has been outstanding against the Giants in his career, allowing four runs over 33 1/3 innings
By afternoon’s end, the Giants were reduced to their most inexperienced, anonymous lineup of the season. Rookie Bryce Eldridge missed a third straight game due to a head laceration, and right fielder Jung Hoo Lee was lifted from the game after fouling a pitch off his groin in the top of the sixth. Eldridge is not expected to play on Monday.
Up next
The Giants will return to Oracle Park for their final six games of the regular season, beginning with a three-game set against the Minnesota Twins.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers playoff roster projection: Could Edwin Díaz, Josue De Paula, even Hyeseong Kim surprise?
item.dc:creator: Jack Harris

item.content:encoded:
Entering the final week of the regular season, the Dodgers more or less know their postseason fate.
They've locked up the National League West. They are a seemingly safe four games clear of the Atlanta Braves for a first-round bye. And, unless they can close a two-game gap on the Milwaukee Brewers without holding the tiebreaker, they will finish as the NL's No. 2 seed, getting home-field advantage at least for the NL Division Series.
Thus, the real intrigue for now is who might be on the Dodgers' postseason roster when the playoffs begin next month.
This year, injuries and fluctuating performances have forced them to cycle 53 different players through their clubhouse.
And while the core of the group is clear, many questions remain about how the club will construct its lineup and pitching staff for this fall's pursuit of a third-straight World Series.
Here is the California Post's best guess about how it will all shake out.
Lineup locks
Will Smith, Freddie Freeman, Tommy Edman, Mookie Betts, Max Muncy, Teoscar Hernández, Andy Pages, Kyle Tucker, Shohei Ohtani, Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia
There won't be any big surprises in how the Dodgers line up to begin the playoffs, assuming Ohtani is healthy enough to resume everyday DH'ing duties.
Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker have cemented their place as everyday hitters thanks to late-season surges. Andy Pages is due back on Tuesday from a fractured hand. Freddie Freeman still seems somewhat limited by his right knee injury, but has nonetheless been able to manage it well enough to this point. And while Tommy Edman has been slumping lately, he doesn't seem to be in immediate danger of losing at-bats.
On the bench, Hunter Feduccia has locked up the back-up catching job, and could be a left-handed hitting option as a pinch-hitter. Kiké Hernández and Miguel Rojas, meanwhile, each provide versatile defensive depth, as well as extensive track records for postseason heroics when called upon.
Entering the final week of the regular season, the core of the Dodgers' position player group looks as they expected.
Dodgers Lineup questions
Bubble candidates: Josue De Paula, Dalton Rushing, Alex Call, Alex Freeland, Hyeseong Kim
The Dodgers will still have one, if not two, position player spots to fill depending on how they construct their roster (i.e. an even 13 pitchers/13 hitters, or a 12/14 split like they used last year?)
And for those, they could have a number of difficult decisions.
First and foremost: Will Josue De Paula make the playoff roster?
If he does, it will likely be as a left-handed bench bat; though if there is any lingering uncertainty with Ohtani, he could also provide insurance as a backup DH option. His main competition right now figures to be Alex Call (who might be redundant to Rojas and Hernández as a right-handed bench bat) or Dalton Rushing (who is an intriguing alternative as a left-handed bat, but remains sidelined from the setback he suffered with his elbow injury earlier this month).
In just 10 MLB games, De Paula has quickly built a strong case, showing supreme plate discipline (10 walks to only four strikeouts) and the potential for power (three doubles, one home run, seven RBIs). At this point, it might be more of a surprise if he doesn't make it.
If the Dodgers elect to carry an extra position player on top of that, the choices are even more varied.
Last year, they rostered two base-running/defensive specialists throughout the playoffs in infielder Hyeseong Kim and outfielder Justin Dean. Dean is now gone, and Hernández could serve as a late-game defensive outfield replacement anyway. But Kim remains in consideration, manager Dave Roberts said, thanks to his speed and infield glove. Alex Freeland could also factor in here, as someone capable of providing more at the plate.
Lineup projection for Los Angeles
C: Will Smith
1B: Freddie Freeman
2B: Tommy Edman
SS: Mookie Betts
3B: Max Muncy
LF: Teoscar Hernández
CF: Andy Pages
RF: Kyle Tucker
DH: Shohei Ohtani
Bench: Kiké Hernández, Miguel Rojas, Hunter Feduccia, Josue De Paula, Hyeseong Kim*
*If the Dodgers carry 14 position players
Dodgers pitching staff locks
Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow, Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips
The Dodgers' starting rotation is set, assuming no further setbacks with Blake Snell's groin injury. The back end of the bullpen has come into focus, too, with Tanner Scott and/or Roki Sasaki the most logical candidates to serve as closer, and Alex Vesia and Evan Phillips separating themselves as the team's next most-trusted high-leverage relief options.
The only real question here is how the Dodgers will line up the rotation. Yamamoto-Skubal would make sense for Games 1 and 2 of a division series (keeping them both on-line for a potential Game 5). But could Tyler Glasnow's potential issues with traveling tempt the Dodgers to use him primarily at home, if they can? All factors to consider in the coming weeks.
Pitching staff questions
Roster bubble candidates: Brock Stewart, Edwin Díaz, Blake Treinen, Kris Bubic, Jack Dreyer, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski, Edgardo Henriquez, Will Klein, Eric Lauer
The first thing the Dodgers need to figure out here is health.
Edgardo Henriquez will almost certainly be on the playoff roster, and pitching in a high-leverage role, if he can make a full recovery from his recent back strain. Will Klein and Eric Lauer might also be available health-wise, though lack clear roles to step immediately back into.
Otherwise, the Dodgers will effectively have at least four open spots for six to seven other pitchers.
For added right-handed depth, they might be deciding between Brock Stewart (who has been a go-to weapon against right-handed hitters recently), Edwin Díaz (who is trying to salvage his dismal debut season, and did throw a pair of scoreless outings this weekend) and Blake Treinen (who has curiously pitched only five times in three weeks since being activated from the injured list, and not in the highest of leverage).
For another left-handed option, they could go with Kris Bubic (the trade deadline acquisition who has impressed with three scoreless appearances since returning from an injury) or Jack Dreyer (who was one of the Dodgers' best relievers from June to August, but has given up five runs in his last seven outings).
And for a multi-inning role, they will have Emmet Sheehan (who has looked like a different pitcher in three sterling starts since returning from a minor-league demotion) and Justin Wrobleski (the breakout All-Star who has finally shaken some of his home run problems since moving to the bullpen).
There are many permutations that the Dodgers could employ depending on opponent. They're still figuring out the exact hierarchy of all their bullpen arms, too.
But as long as their rotation is dominant, everything else should take care of itself.
Pitching staff projection
Rotation: Yoshinobu Yamamoto, Tarik Skubal, Blake Snell, Tyler Glasnow
Bullpen: Roki Sasaki, Tanner Scott, Alex Vesia, Evan Phillips, Brock Stewart, Kris Bubic, Edwin Díaz, Emmet Sheehan, Justin Wrobleski

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Dodgers have lineup problem they cannot afford to solve by benching Josue De Paula
item.dc:creator: Miracle Dimwesh
item.description: Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore. De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason. That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula was supposed to give the Los Angeles Dodgers another young bat for the final weeks of the regular season. Instead, the rookie has created a lineup problem the team may not be able to ignore.
De Paula has been too productive to simply remove from the lineup. The 21-year-old has reached base at a .474 clip through his first 10 MLB games, giving the Dodgers another dangerous left-handed hitter before the postseason.
That creates an interesting problem when Shohei Ohtani returns. The Dodgers have several established outfielders, but De Paula's bat is making it harder to find room for everyone.
Josue De Paula has been doing this all year
The rookie's hot start is not coming out of nowhere. De Paula dominated Double-A pitching throughout the season before earning his September call-up.
Minor League Baseball named him the 2026 Texas League MVP on Monday. He hit .303/.401/.547 with 27 home runs, 31 stolen bases, 152 hits and 104 RBIs in 124 games for Tulsa.
That production earned him a direct jump from Double-A to Los Angeles. He has continued showing the same offensive approach against MLB pitching.
De Paula has gone 8-for-28 with 10 walks, one home run and seven RBIs in his first 10 games. He has also played two games in left field, showing the Dodgers can move him around when necessary.
Dodgers face a difficult Ohtani lineup decision
Feb 24, 2026; Phoenix, Arizona, USA; Los Angeles Dodgers outfielder Josue De Paula against the Cleveland Guardians during a spring training game at Camelback Ranch-Glendale. Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters)
The situation becomes more complicated with Ohtani nearing a return. Manager Dave Roberts said there is a good chance Ohtani will be activated Wednesday against the San Diego Padres. He will return as a hitter, not a pitcher.
That puts Ohtani back at DH and removes the easiest path to keeping De Paula in the lineup.
The Dodgers already have Kyle Tucker in right field, Teoscar Hernández in left and Andy Pages in center. Tucker signed a four-year, $240 million deal before the season, while Hernández and Pages have remained important parts of the club's outfield plans.
De Paula can play the outfield, but moving him there would force another decision. Taking one of the established outfielders out also means changing a group that has helped Los Angeles reach this point.
The Dodgers do not have to solve the entire problem today. But De Paula's performance has made one thing clear: when Ohtani returns, finding enough at-bats for everyone will be one of Dave Roberts' biggest lineup challenges heading into October.

item.title: [Yahoo Sports] Josue De Paula's Early Success Might Be Bad News For This Dodgers Veteran
item.dc:creator: Aaliyan Mohammed
item.description: The Los Angeles Dodgers called Josue De Paula up from Double-A earlier this month, and he has been making headlines with his bat early on. It was the first time under Andrew Friedman that the Dodgers called a position player up directly from Double-A. De Paula's defense is not great, but Shohei Ohtani being injured has allowed him to serve as the designated hitter. item.content:encoded:
The Los Angeles Dodgers called Josue De Paula up from Double-A earlier this month, and he has been making headlines with his bat early on.
It was the first time under Andrew Friedman that the Dodgers called a position player up directly from Double-A. De Paula's defense is not great, but Shohei Ohtani being injured has allowed him to serve as the designated hitter.
In 10 games, he is slashing .286/.474/.500 with half of his hits going for extra bases. His bat and eye at the plate have been as advertised. He is the Dodgers' top prospect and the No. 6 prospect in baseball. He won't be eligible for the postseason since he was not on the 40-man roster by Sept. 1, but his future for the Dodgers looks bright,
He is bound to slump at some point, but his early success means even if he is in Triple-A to start the season next year, it won't be long for him to be back with the big league club. However, Ohtani will be back, and De Paula will need a spot in the outfield. Unfortunately for Teoscar Hernández, he is the most likely to lose his job to De Paula.
Hernández has one year left on his contract, and his OPS has taken a big dive after his All-Star season in 2024. De Paula has shined with the bat and is working hard to improve his defense. If he can do that, he should take Hernández's spot.
What would that mean for Hernández? Well, it's not really the Dodgers' style to trade away their own stars, but De Paula needs to play. Hernández is about to be 34, and he still has trade value. He is not a great defender, so if De Paula is going to replace one of the Dodgers' starting outfielders, it's going to be the one who also isn't great defensively and is old. Kyle Tucker and Andy Pages are not going anywhere.
It's unclear what the Dodgers will do with De Paula next year. They've seen that his bat is ready for the big leagues, but may still want him to get some Triple-A work before making him an every day player in the big leagues. Eventually, he will start to slump in the Majors, like every young hitter, and will have to make adjustments. Regardless, his early success is a threat to Hernández's future with the team.
More MLB: Paul Skenes Reveals Whether World Baseball Classic Is To Blame For Down Year

item.title: [Dodgers Way] Mookie Betts' sudden revival could be Dodgers' secret weapon in securing three-peat
item.dc:creator: Brandon Glick
item.description: The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start. item.content:encoded:
The death of Mookie Betts at the plate appears to have been greatly exaggerated. The eight-time All-Star certainly won't be able to consider his 2026 campaign alongside some of his historic performances from years past, but he's put together another strong season after a calamitous start.
Specifically since August 17, he's been one of the best hitters in all of baseball. He leads the Los Angeles Dodgers in all three triple-slash categories (.336/.427/.611), wRC+ (183), home runs (seven), RBI (27), and fWAR (2.0) from that point forward, emerging at a time when the team has gotten all of 71 plate appearances (and a 101 wRC+) from Shohei Ohtani.
Betts isn't a "secret weapon" by traditional standards; his MVP credentials and three World Series rings would certainly beg to differ. But after he struggled mightily a year ago and then followed that up with an even worse encore at the beginning of 2026, having him healthy and in his best groove in years could be the deciding factor in the Dodgers' quest for a three-peat.
Mookie Betts has elevated his own floor and with it, the Dodgers' ceiling
The Dodgers are hardly hurting for production, ranking third in the league in runs scored since mid-August. Even without Ohtani, they can batter opposing pitching staffs with their depth, especially now that Kyle Tucker finally looks interested in participating in this group project.
But more than a rejuvenated Tucker or red-hot Teoscar Hernández, there's something special about Betts in particular getting this hot. He's the fourth-longest tenured player on the roster, surpassed by only Max Muncy and Will Smith among position players. He's been around for each of the three recent championships, posting a cumulative OPS over .800 in those playoff runs.
One of the most selfless superstars you'll ever find, there's a "you go, we go" aura that orbits Betts, especially now that he's reclaimed his rightful spot atop the batting order as Dave Roberts' leadoff hitter. His all-around talents lengthen the lineup to a tremendous degree, something opposing pitchers will really feel once Ohtani is back in the fold.
It's not all perfect, of course. His hard-hit rate even during this hot streak is well below the figures he'd post in his prime, and he's still hitting a few too many balls on the ground. Naturally, all of his expected stats during this stretch fall shy of his actual results, including significant disparities in his slugging percentage (.611 compared to a .458 xSLG) and wOBA (.443 compared to a .374 xwOBA).
Those expected metrics are still leaps and bounds better than we got earlier this season, though, and that's the real takeaway here. Even if Betts can't keep this MVP-caliber charade going through all of October, he's clearly found a more stable baseline level of performance that can still help the Dodgers win.

item.title: [Dodger Blue] Josue De Paula responds to criticism about defense with bold prediction
item.dc:creator: Blake Williams
item.description: Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut. Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level. But his defense in the outfield is a m
item.content:encoded:
Josue De Paula has been everything the Los Angeles Dodgers could have hoped for in the batter’s box during since getting called up for his MLB debut.
Since being added onto the Dodgers roster to replace Shohei Ohtani as the everyday designated hitter, De Paula has shown off his patience, ability to take a quality at-bat, and power and speed combination. The sky is the limit for De Paula’s offensive capabilities, and that’s what carried him to the MLB level.
But his defense in the outfield is a major area of concern, and it’s part of the reason the Dodgers did not call De Paula up until needing a regular DH. As they look ahead to the postseason, De Paula is likely to be limited to being a bat off the bench, given his defensive struggles and the uptick of production from Teoscar Hernández and Kyle Tucker.
However, De Paula knows he needs to improve in the outfield, and he’s made it a focus during his first stint at the MLB level.
“Every day. I know that’s a big area of improvement for me, and I know I’ve got a lot of hate on it,” De Paula said. “I’m the type that if I get hate on it, I’m going to focus on it more. I’m going to shut a lot of people up with my defense very soon.”
De Paula has spent time before every game practicing his defense, working with Dodgers coaches to become more of a usable option in the outfield. Dodgers manager Dave Roberts has taken notice of that, and issued a challenge to De Paula.
“Well, it’s clear he needs to improve on his defense,” Roberts said. “How do you shut people up? You perform better. You practice hard, and that’s how you do it. My challenge to him is to be a complete baseball player, and not just to be a hitter. So he’s putting a lot of good work with Dino every day, and so I welcome that.”
Josue De Paula praises Dodgers teammates
De Paula became the first position player promoted from Double-A by Dodgers president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman, creating lofty expectations for himself.
The 21-year-old has felt prepared to meet the challenge of playing in the Majors head-on and credits his Dodgers teammates for creating an environment conducive to letting him play freely.
“Probably the biggest is takeaway is it’s basically the same game, just around different people,” De Paula said on SportsNet LA. “But one thing I didn’t expect was this team to be so cool. Like, all the players, the way they accepted me, the way they greeted me, making me feel comfortable. It put me in a better position to be me.”

item.title: [sbsun.com] Emmet Sheehan strengthens postseason case as Dodgers sweep Giants
item.dc:creator: Bill Plunkett
item.description: LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece. Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep. item.content:encoded:
LOS ANGELES — Hiding behind that 5.00 ERA Emmet Sheehan toted around for much of the season might have been a valuable postseason piece.
Sheehan allowed just one hit in 5⅓ scoreless innings on Sunday afternoon as the Dodgers beat the San Francisco Giants, 3-1, to complete a three-game sweep.
Sheehan retired 16 of the 18 batters he faced, allowing just one single and walking one while striking out nine.
“I’ve loved the version we’ve seen of Emmet the last three outings,” Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said. “He’s been fantastic.
“We’ve seen confidence. We’ve seen when you’re essentially fighting for your life to create an opportunity for yourself. That’s what I see. There’s urgency. I like the way that he’s trusting his stuff. He’s in a good spot physically, and you know the performance has been fantastic.”
The outing was Sheehan’s third consecutive outstanding performance this month as he has bounced between Triple-A and the majors. It cemented a spot in the Dodgers’ postseason bullpen after a rough season for the 26-year-old right-hander – an outcome that did not seem likely when he was demoted to Triple-A in early August.
“I don’t know that I proved anything to myself. It was just getting a couple things right and I think I’m in a much better spot now,” Sheehan said.
“My confidence stayed the same the whole time. I knew the coaches down there were going to help me and I was going to get right. I took that approach going into it. I wasn’t helping the team here so I needed that a little bit.”
Sheehan has been called up for two starts this month and pitched in ‘bulk’ following Jack Dreyer as an opener on Sunday. Sheehan carried a 5.29 ERA into September after 20 starts for the Dodgers that landed him back in the minors.
In his three September outings, though, Sheehan has shown rediscovered fastball command after working on his delivery in Triple-A. He has allowed just one run in 17 innings, holding hitters to a .105 average (6 for 57) with 24 strikeouts and three walks. After giving up 20 home runs in those first 20 starts, he has allowed just one in his 17 September innings.
If his confidence didn’t need repair, his delivery and pitch mix needed some work.
Now two years removed from Tommy John surgery, Sheehan was thrown by not quite having recovered all of his fastball velocity this year. When he chased those extra miles per hour, it was counterproductive. He has become more comfortable at 94-95 mph now.
“I think it’s a few things,” he said Sunday. “Definitely … being more comfortable in my delivery, being out there staying free and easy with everything, not trying to do too much. Instead of saying, ‘I need 97 here.’ It’s more like ‘If I hit my spot, he’s not going to hit it.’”
They haven’t. Sheehan has gotten 50 swings-and-misses in his three outings this month, nearly half of them (24) on his reborn four-seam fastball. He also got six on his curveball on Sunday.
“That’s something that (assistant pitching coach) Connor (McGuinness), (pitching coach) Mark (Prior) and I and the coaches down in Triple-A have been working on is just expanding the front-to-back game with the fastball and the curveball,” Sheehan said. “I think some guys ended up throughout the season sitting mid-speed, slider-changeup, on me. Having that change of speeds the last couple has been very important.”
The Dodgers moved Sheehan to the bullpen for the postseason last October and saw him as a big weapon in that role. The results were mixed, however, in part because of some pitch tipping issues which Sheehan said have been addressed. He will be wiser this time around, he said.
“Definitely,” Sheehan said. “I think the routine of everything can be a little bit hard to adjust to right away. So having that experience helps a lot. Just getting back into that, I know what I need to do to get ready to go into the game.”
The Dodgers gave him a little bit of a test drive by using Dreyer as an ‘opener’ before him. The Giants scratched out one run in the first inning against Dreyer when he walked leadoff man Jonah Cox. Cox moved to second base on a wild pickoff attempt by Dreyer, stole third and scored on Victor Bericoto’s RBI single. The Giants had just one more hit in the game.
“I think that obviously there’s a 97 that plays better, but 94-95 commanded still misses bats,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who will rejoin Oklahoma City for the Triple-A playoffs this week before returning to the Dodgers for the postseason. “That’s one part of it. The other part of it is holding the velocity. And so, for me, the last three or four since he’s been back here, he’s held those 94s and 95s for the, call it 85 pitches.”
The Giants’ run against Dreyer stood up as the only run of the day until Tommy Edman emerged from a 2-for-41 slump to hit a solo home run in the sixth inning.
The Dodgers broke the 1-1 tie in the seventh on singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula followed by an RBI double from Kiké Hernandez.
They stranded De Paula and Hernandez in scoring position, but singles by Teoscar Hernandez, Freddie Freeman and Muncy produced another run in the eighth inning.
Kris Bubic, Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott combined on 2⅔ innings of hitless relief to close out the combined two-hitter for the Dodgers’ 96th win. With the win, the Dodgers’ magic number to clinch a first-round bye over the Atlanta Braves (who clinched the National League East division title on Sunday) dropped to three with six games left in the regular season.
The Dodgers (96-60) remain two games behind the Milwaukee Brewers (98-58) for the top seed, though the Brewers also hold the head-to-head tiebreaker. The No. 3 seed – currently Atlanta (92-64) – will play host to a best-of-three Wild Card Series against either the Chicago Cubs (87-69), San Diego Padres (87-69) or Philadelphia Phillies (86-70).

item.title: [bignewsnetwork.com] Emmet Sheehan dominates Giants in long relief as Dodgers cap sweep
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.description: Emmet Sheehan dominates Giants in long relief as Dodgers cap sweep (Photo credit: William Liang) Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and the Los Angeles Dodgers completed a three-game home sweep of the rival San Francisco Giants with a 3-1 victory Sunday afternoon. Tommy Edman homered for Los Angeles (96-60), which won its fourth straight and remained four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (92-64) in the race fo
item.content:encoded:
Emmet Sheehan dominates Giants in long relief as Dodgers cap sweep
(Photo credit: William Liang)
Emmet Sheehan pitched brilliantly in long relief, Enrique Hernandez broke a seventh-inning tie with a run-scoring double and the Los Angeles Dodgers completed a three-game home sweep of the rival San Francisco Giants with a 3-1 victory Sunday afternoon.
Tommy Edman homered for Los Angeles (96-60), which won its fourth straight and remained four games ahead of the Atlanta Braves (92-64) in the race for the National League's No. 2 seed and a first-round bye in the playoffs.
After Victor Bericoto had singled home Jonah Cox in the first inning against Dodgers opener Jack Dreyer, Sheehan took over to start the second and held the Giants to just one hit over the next 5 1/3 scoreless innings. Nine of the 16 outs he recorded came via strikeout.
Meanwhile, Edman's homer, his seventh of the season, produced a 1-1 tie in the sixth. It came off Giants reliever Carson Seymour, who had replaced Matt Wilkinson after five shutout innings.
Making his fifth career start, Wilkinson limited the Dodgers to three hits while striking out six.
The clubs took the 1-1 tie into the bottom of the seventh, when one-out singles by Max Muncy and Josue De Paula off Sam Hentges (1-7) set the stage for Hernandez, whose double to center field drove in the go-ahead run.
Muncy provided an insurance run with an RBI single in the eighth that scored Teoscar Hernandez, who had singled.
Kris Bubic (4-2), Brock Stewart and Tanner Scott threw the final 2 2/3 innings for the Dodgers, allowing just two baserunners, one on an error and the other via a walk.
Scott walked Brett Harris with two outs in the ninth, bringing the potential tying run to the plate. But the left-hander locked down his 23rd save by striking out Osleivis Basabe.
Muncy, De Paula, Teoscar Hernandez and Freddie Freeman had two hits apiece for the Dodgers, who will host the second-place San Diego Padres for three games before closing the regular season with three in San Francisco beginning Friday.
Jung Hoo Lee joined Bericoto with the only hits for the Giants (64-92), who completed their road schedule with a 28-53 record.
--Field Level Media

item.title: [Los Angeles Times] Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
item.dc:creator: Kevin Baxter
item.description: Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants - Click here to listen to this article - Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292. The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National
item.content:encoded:
Is it still a rivalry? Dodgers complete sweep of woeful Giants
- Click here to listen to this article
-
Only the Pirates and Cubs have met more often than the Dodgers and Giants, who faced off for the first time in 1889. And over all that time, the Dodgers are just two games better, with 1,294 wins to the Giants’ 1,292.
The Dodgers and Giants have also won more pennants, made more World Series appearances and have more players wearing their caps in the Hall of Fame than any other National League teams, all of which fueled a rivalry that was once among the most visceral and passionate in American sports.
But that was then and this is now.
After Sunday’s 3-1 victory over the Giants, the Dodgers’ 14th win in their last 17 games, the team could finish a season with 100 wins for the fourth time in six years. The Giants have had just one winning record in that time.
The Dodgers (96-60), who have won five straight division titles, are headed to the postseason for a record-tying 14th consecutive year. The Giants will miss the playoffs for a fifth straight season.
So is the rivalry dead? That depends on who you ask.
“It’s always a rivalry,” Giants pitcher Logan Webb. “We’d like to make it a little closer when it comes to the standings. But I definitely feel it when I throw against them.”
But then Webb, who is from Northern California, grew up with the rivalry and, as the longest-tenured Giant, pitched against the Dodgers in games that mattered. Giants coach Ron Washington, who made his major league debut with the Dodgers when the rivalry was still a thing, said many players on San Francisco’s roster don’t know that background.
Mookie Betts hits three doubles and the Dodgers piled up 15 hits in a 10-4 win over the San Francisco Giants with Shohei Ohtani’s return on the horizon.
“It should be a rivalry. But I don’t think the young kids we got know anything about a rivalry. They’re not history buffs.”
Webb said it’s the responsibility of the veterans on both sides to keep that history alive by explaining the enmity to the young players.
“I think there are still guys that came up in the system that know what it’s like,” he said. “It’s my job to kind of hype these guys up to play a game like this.”
Dodgers manager Dave Roberts, who played for the Dodgers and Giants during his 10-year career, agrees the rivalry now exists more in the history books than the current standings, where the Giants have been overtaken by the San Diego Padres, who will finish second to the Dodgers in the N.L. West for the fourth time in five seasons.
“It’s certainly a rivalry in the sense of the history, the fan bases,” Roberts said. “But obviously it’s about relevancy. The Padres have been successful the last handful of years, and so it’s certainly built some momentum. The geography lends itself to that too.
“But Dodgers Giants is always fun.”
It hasn’t been so much fun for the Giants lately. San Francisco hasn’t won the season series with the Dodgers since 2021 and has lost more than 90 games this year for the first time in nine seasons.
On Sunday they went in front three batters into the game with Johan Cox working Dodger opener Jack Dreyer for a leadoff walk, then making his way around the bases on Dreyer’s throwing error, a stolen base and a one-one single by Victor Bericoto.
But San Francisco didn’t get another hit until Jung Hoo Lee singled with one out in the sixth.
That allowed the Dodgers to tie the score in the sixth on Tommy Edman’s seventh home run of the season just inside the right-field foul pole. An inning later they went ahead to stay when Max Muncy singled under a sliding Cox at second, moved to third on a single by rookie Josue De Paula and scored on Kiké Hernández’s double to center.
A two-out single by Muncy, his second of the game, scored Teoscar Hernández, who also had two hits, in the eighth inning with the final run.
Even the slumping Freddie Freeman contributed to the Dodgers’ 11-hit attack, ending an 0-for-11 slide with a broken-bat single in the fourth then singling again in the eighth.
Sunday’s result helped clarify the Dodgers’ once-muddy playoff picture. With six games left in the regular season, the Dodgers lead Atlanta by four games in the race for the second seed in the National League playoffs, which would give them a first-round bye and the homefield advantage in the division series.
The team’s postseason roster may be getting clearer as well. Right-hander Emmet Sheehan, who made 22 starts this season, came out of the bullpen for the first time Sunday and was brilliant in his audition for the playoffs.
“If there is a role in the postseason, it will be out of the [bull]pen,” Roberts said of Sheehan, who gave up just a hit and walk, striking out nine — one off his season high — in 5 1/3 innings.
Tyler Glasnow hasn’t had the greatest of seasons, but the Dodgers will need him to deliver in the playoffs if they want to win another World Series title.
De Paula, meanwhile, who also doubled in running his modest hitting streak to four games, appears to have secured a job as the team’s left-handed bat off the bench while utility player Hyeseong Kim, who has spent the last four months in the minors, will rejoin the Dodgers after the triple-A playoffs and be considered for a roster spot as a pinch-runner and late-inning defensive replacement.
“My expectation is that Hyeseong will be here during the off week and potentially be a conversation for the postseason because he has the ability to run, play defense, and steal a base,” Roberts said.
After Monday’s off day, the final break of the regular season for the Dodgers, the team is expected to activate Andy Pages, Roki Sasaki and Shohei Ohtani from the injured list during its three-game series with the Padres.

item.title: [Sports Illustrated] Dodgers Manager Makes Surprise Admission About Mookie Betts' Resurgence

item.content:encoded:
Los Angeles Dodgers shortstop Mookie Betts led off in manager Dave Roberts' lineup for the third consecutive game Sunday against the San Francisco Giants. Betts looks immovable right now, especially on the heels of a game in which he reached base five times. He collected three doubles, a single and a walk in the Dodgers' 10-4 win on Saturday at Dodger Stadium.
Betts' September surge marks an abrupt change from the five months that came before.
Through the end of August, Betts' .701 OPS ranked 123rd out of 163 major league hitters with at least 400 plate appearances. Since Sept. 1, his OPS was an outstanding 1.287 entering Sunday, trailing only Cincinnati Reds shortstop Elly De La Cruz among 181 qualified hitters this month.
"I couldn’t tell you that I saw this,” Roberts said Saturday, referring to Betts' dramatic turnaround. “But I just felt that he was stronger. He’s worked hard on that. He looks great. He’s not going to stop working, and just for it to come together has been great.”
The Dodgers will have a choice to make if and when Shohei Ohtani returns from the injured list. Ostensibly he'll go back to the leadoff spot again, though his health — and Betts' resurgence — are at least making it a conversation.
For the Dodgers, it's a good problem to have at the right time.
At 33, Betts is facing many of the same questions the Dodgers' other 30-and-over stars face anytime their performance slips. Has age caught up to them? Can they maintain their performance through the end of October? Do the Dodgers need a younger player to take their place in order to repeat as World Series champions?
The questions apply to Miguel Rojas (37), Freddie Freeman (36), Max Muncy (35), Kiké Hernández (34), Teoscar Hernández (33), Tommy Edman (31) and Ohtani (31), as well as Betts.
Professional athletes are famously the last to know when their physical skills are no longer enough to justify their roster spot. Take it with a grain of salt, but Betts isn't worried about his ability to maintain his current stretch of play.
“I mean this is it,” Betts said of his recent form. “I know I’m still capable of it, it’s in there somewhere. So, just gotta keep on rolling, keep on laying the foundation and letting the game be the game.”
Sign up for our free newsletter and follow us on X/Twitter and Facebook for the latest news.
J.P. Hoornstra is an On SI Contributor. A veteran of 20 years of sports coverage for daily newspapers in California, J.P. covered MLB, the Los Angeles Dodgers, and the Los Angeles Angels (occasionally of Anaheim) from 2012-23 for the Southern California News Group. His first book, The 50 Greatest Dodgers Games of All-Time, published in 2015. In 2016, he won an Associated Press Sports Editors award for breaking news coverage. He once recorded a keyboard solo on the same album as two of the original Doors.

item.description: Kyle Tucker has started to heat up at the perfect time for the Los Angeles Dodgers. Signed this past offseason to a massive four-year, $240 million deal, he spent most of the summer struggling at the plate and unable to string together any consistent production.
